examples.zh: 國小在百年校慶當天埋下一只不銹鋼時空膠囊，裡面封存著全體學生的夢想作文，約定五十年後開箱啟封。

entries.definition: 膠囊；太空艙；承受四萬公里時速大氣層再入之耐高溫採樣返回艙

explains.en: This noun can mean a small container, often one that holds medicine. It can also mean a small spacecraft or a short summary of information. The shape is usually compact and enclosed.
A person swallows a small shell that contains medicine. The shell dissolves inside the body. It holds a dose of medicine.
A spacecraft carries astronauts between Earth and space. A news report may also give a short summary in a few lines. The noun has several uses.

examples.en: Write a witty caption for your travel photo on Instagram.
examples.zh: 在 Instagram 上為你的旅遊風景美照寫一段幽默有趣的圖說。

examples.en: Closed captions make televised news accessible to hearing-impaired viewers.
examples.zh: 隱藏式字幕讓聽障觀眾也能順暢無礙地接收電視新聞資訊。

examples.en: The historical photo caption detailed the exact date and location of the signing.
examples.zh: 這張歷史老照片下方的圖說清楚標註了簽約的確切日期與歷史地點。

examples.en: Detailed bilingual wall captions provide artist biographies, creation years, and medium specifications.
examples.zh: 展牆上張貼的詳盡中英雙語展品說明卡，清楚標示出藝術家生平傳記、創作年代、畫布材質與尺寸。

examples.en: She leaned close to read the tiny printed caption beside the ancient Egyptian burial scarab.
examples.zh: 她俯下身子湊近展櫃，仔細閱讀陳列在古埃及聖甲蟲護身符旁印製工整的微型文物說明標牌。

examples.en: The documentary film features English subtitles and clear audio descriptions alongside informative captions.
examples.zh: 這部獲獎的文化紀錄片除了配備詳盡的知識解說字幕外，亦提供英文同步字幕與視障語音口述影像輔助。

entries.definition: 圖說；隱藏字幕 (CC)；說明文字；展品解說標牌說明卡；字幕

explains.en: This noun means a short piece of text that explains a picture or gives words for a video. It can also be the title of a legal case. The context shows the meaning.
A photo in a newspaper has a sentence beneath it saying where it was taken. The sentence explains the image. It gives useful information.
A video may show written words so viewers can read what people say. A picture book may also have a short note under each image. The noun names these texts.

examples.en: The captive bird was released into the forest.
examples.zh: 那隻被關起來的鳥被放回森林。

examples.en: The story follows a captive who plans an escape.
examples.zh: 故事描寫一名被俘者計畫逃脫。

examples.en: The speaker had a captive audience on the bus.
examples.zh: 演講者在公車上有一群無法離開的聽眾。

entries.definition: 俘虜；被囚禁者；受控制的；被吸引住的。

explains.en: This adjective describes a person or animal kept from leaving a place. As a noun, it means someone held in this way. The word often appears in stories about rescue or war.
A bird is kept inside a cage and cannot fly away. It has no freedom to leave. The adjective describes its situation.
A person held by an enemy may be called this. In a less literal use, an audience may be unable to leave easily. The word describes being held or unable to go.

examples.en: The rescued eagle recovered after years in captivity.
examples.zh: 獲救的老鷹在多年遭囚禁後逐漸復原。

examples.en: The story tells of a family’s captivity during the war.
examples.zh: 故事描述一家人在戰爭期間遭囚禁的經歷。

examples.en: The animal was returned to the wild after captivity.
examples.zh: 那隻動物在遭囚禁後被送回野外。

entries.definition: （名）囚禁；被俘狀態；受控制的狀態

explains.en: This noun means the condition of being held and unable to leave. It can describe people or animals. The word often appears in stories, history, and news.
A wild animal is kept in a cage instead of living in its natural home. It cannot move freely. This is a state of confinement.
A person may be held by an enemy during a conflict. The person has lost freedom to leave. The noun describes that state.

examples.en: The books arrived in a cardboard box.
examples.zh: 書本裝在紙板箱裡送到。

examples.en: We made a cardboard model of the house.
examples.zh: 我們用厚紙板做了一個房子的模型。

examples.en: Please recycle the cardboard after unpacking.
examples.zh: 拆開包裝後請回收紙板。

explains.en: This noun means thick, stiff paper used for boxes and signs. It is made from layers of paper and can be recycled. The adjective describes something made from this material.
A shipping box is strong enough to hold books but can be cut with scissors. The thick paper is useful for boxes. It is stronger than ordinary paper.
A child makes a toy castle from flat brown sheets. The sheets fold and hold their shape. The word can name the material or describe the castle.

examples.en: Honesty is a cardinal rule in the game.
examples.zh: 誠實是這場遊戲的一項基本原則。

examples.en: A cardinal sang from the maple tree.
examples.zh: 一隻紅衣主教鳥在楓樹上鳴唱。

examples.en: The cardinal spoke at the church service.
examples.zh: 樞機主教在教會禮拜中致詞。

entries.definition: （名）紅衣主教；（形）最重要的、基本的。

explains.en: This adjective means most important or basic. As a noun, it can mean a senior church leader or a bright red bird found in North America. Context tells which meaning is intended.
A rule says never share a password with strangers. It is a very important rule. The adjective describes its high importance.
A red bird with a crest visits a backyard feeder. A senior church leader may hold this title. The noun has these separate meanings.

examples.en: They spent a carefree day at the beach.
examples.zh: 他們在海邊度過了無憂無慮的一天。

examples.en: Her carefree laugh filled the room.
examples.zh: 她無拘無束的笑聲充滿了房間。

examples.en: He remembered his carefree childhood summers.
examples.zh: 他想起童年那些無憂無慮的夏日。

explains.en: This adjective describes someone who feels free from worry or heavy responsibility. It can also describe a relaxed time or manner. It does not mean a person never has problems.
Children run through a field on a sunny afternoon without thinking about chores. They feel relaxed and happy. The adjective describes their mood.
A person takes a short holiday and enjoys the day without checking work messages. The time feels easy and light. The word describes this relaxed feeling.

examples.en: The caretaker unlocked the school gate at dawn.
examples.zh: 管理員在清晨打開學校大門。

examples.en: A caretaker watered the plants while we were away.
examples.zh: 我們不在時，一位照料者幫忙澆植物。

examples.en: The caretaker government served until the election.
examples.zh: 看守政府執政到選舉為止。

entries.definition: （名）照料者；看守人；代理負責人

explains.en: This noun means a person who looks after a building, property, or someone who needs help. It can also mean a temporary leader who keeps things running. The exact role depends on what is being cared for.
A worker opens a school each morning, checks the rooms, and fixes small problems. The worker looks after the building. This person maintains the place.
A neighbor feeds an older person’s cat while they are away. The neighbor cares for the pet. A temporary manager may also hold this role.

examples.en: The milk carton was empty.
examples.zh: 牛奶紙盒是空的。

examples.en: She bought a carton of eggs at the market.
examples.zh: 她在市場買了一盒雞蛋。

examples.en: The juice carton has a picture of oranges.
examples.zh: 果汁紙盒上有橘子的圖片。

explains.en: This noun means a box or container made from paperboard or light plastic. It often holds milk, juice, eggs, or other food. The shape and material depend on what it carries.
A family pours milk from a sealed paper container into a glass. The container has a folded top. It is a paper package.
Eggs are often packed in a shaped paper container that protects them. A small box of juice is another kind of package. The noun names these containers.

examples.en: The polite cashier scanned the items quickly and handed me the receipt.
examples.zh: 有禮貌的收銀員快速掃描商品並把收據遞給我。

examples.en: She worked part-time as a supermarket cashier during college.
examples.zh: 她在大學求學期間在超級市場擔任兼職收銀員。

examples.en: The customer handed the cash payment directly to the cashier.
examples.zh: 顧客將現金付款直接交給了收銀台出納人員。

explains.en: This noun means a person who takes payment from customers in a shop or restaurant. The worker may use a register and give change. Some businesses also use self-service machines.
A customer places groceries on a counter and pays for them. The worker scans the items and takes the money. This person handles payment.
The worker can accept cash, cards, or other payment methods. The job often involves helping customers at the end of a purchase. This role is common in shops.

examples.en: The crash caused one casualty and several injuries.
examples.zh: 這場事故造成一人傷亡，另有數人受傷。

examples.en: The storm had no human casualties.
examples.zh: 這場風暴沒有人員傷亡。

examples.en: The old bridge was a casualty of the flood.
examples.zh: 老橋在洪水中嚴重受損。

entries.definition: （名）傷亡者；事故、災難或衝突中的受傷或死亡者。

explains.en: This noun means a person killed or injured in an accident, disaster, or conflict. It can also mean a serious loss or failure. News reports often use it when describing harm.
A storm causes a building to fall, and several people are hurt. Each injured person is counted among those harmed. The word can refer to someone hurt or killed.
A company loses a large part of its business after a fire. The event causes a serious loss. The noun can be used for people or for something badly affected.

examples.en: The earthquake was a catastrophe for the small town.
examples.zh: 地震對這座小鎮造成了大災難。

examples.en: The team worked together after the catastrophe.
examples.zh: 災難發生後，團隊一起努力。

examples.en: A fire can become a catastrophe in dry weather.
examples.zh: 天氣乾燥時，火災可能演變成大災難。

entries.definition: 大災難；災禍；極嚴重的失敗。

explains.en: This noun means a sudden event that causes great damage or suffering. It may affect one person, a town, or many people. The result is much worse than expected.
A strong storm destroys homes and roads. Many families lose their belongings. The event is a disaster.
A mistake causes a whole plan to fail. People must deal with serious harm. The noun describes a very bad event.

examples.en: They hired a local company to cater the wedding.
examples.zh: 他們雇用當地公司為婚禮提供餐飲。

examples.en: The small cafe caters to people who work nearby.
examples.zh: 這間小咖啡館主要服務附近上班的人。

examples.en: The menu caters for both adults and children.
examples.zh: 這份菜單同時迎合大人和孩子的需求。

explains.en: This verb can mean to provide food and service for an event. It can also mean to give a person or group what they want. The meaning depends on the situation.
A restaurant prepares meals for a wedding party. Staff bring food to the guests. The business provides food for the event.
A shop offers many simple meals for children. It tries to meet their tastes. The verb can describe serving a certain group.

examples.en: A caterpillar ate holes in the cabbage leaves.
examples.zh: 毛毛蟲把高麗菜葉咬出許多洞。

examples.en: The child watched a caterpillar crawl up the stem.
examples.zh: 孩子看著毛毛蟲沿著莖往上爬。

examples.en: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly after a time.
examples.zh: 過了一段時間，毛毛蟲會變成蝴蝶。

explains.en: This noun means the worm-shaped young form of a butterfly or moth. It has many small legs and eats leaves. Later, it changes into an adult insect.
A green insect crawls along a garden plant. It has eaten several leaves. It is the young form of a butterfly.
Children may find one on a branch in spring. It can have stripes or bright colors. The creature will later change its shape.

examples.en: The dentist found a cavity in my back tooth.
examples.zh: 牙醫發現我後方的牙齒有蛀洞。

examples.en: A small cavity formed inside the old tree.
examples.zh: 老樹裡形成了一個小空洞。

examples.en: The scan showed a cavity in the rock.
examples.zh: 掃描顯示岩石內有個空腔。

entries.definition: （名）洞穴、空腔；物體內部的空洞，也指蛀牙形成的洞。

explains.en: This noun means an empty space or hole inside something. In health, it often means a damaged hole in a tooth. It may be small or large.
A dentist finds a dark spot in a tooth. The spot has become a hole. It may need treatment.
A bird may nest inside a hollow tree. The empty space protects it from rain. The noun can name such an inner space.

examples.en: She chopped celery for the chicken soup.
examples.zh: 她把芹菜切碎，準備煮雞湯。

examples.en: I put celery sticks in my lunch box.
examples.zh: 我把芹菜條放進便當盒。

examples.en: Celery has a crisp texture when it is fresh.
examples.zh: 新鮮芹菜吃起來口感爽脆。

entries.definition: 芹菜；可食用的脆莖蔬菜。

explains.en: This noun names a crisp green plant with long pale stalks and leaves. People eat it raw or cooked. It has a mild taste and a lot of water.
A cook cuts the stalks into small pieces for soup. They soften as they heat. The vegetable adds a fresh taste.
Someone packs a few sticks with lunch. They may add a dip or eat them plain. The plant is often used in salads.

examples.en: The lab studied cellular changes in the plant.
examples.zh: 實驗室研究了植物細胞的變化。

examples.en: We lost cellular service in the valley.
examples.zh: 我們在山谷裡收不到行動電話訊號。

examples.en: Cellular networks connect phones across the country.
examples.zh: 行動電話網路讓手機能在全國各地連線。

entries.definition: （形）細胞的；蜂巢狀的；行動電話的

explains.en: This adjective can describe something made of or related to tiny living parts. It can also describe a phone system that sends signals between nearby towers. The topic tells which sense is meant.
A science lesson looks at how living parts grow and divide. The teacher uses a microscope image. The lesson concerns the basic units of life.
A phone connects to a nearby tower while someone drives. The call can continue as the signal moves between towers. The adjective describes this kind of network.

examples.en: The water reached 100 degrees Celsius.
examples.zh: 水溫達到攝氏一百度。

examples.en: It was five degrees Celsius outside this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上外面是攝氏五度。

examples.en: The weather may rise to 30 degrees Celsius today.
examples.zh: 今天氣溫可能升到攝氏三十度。

explains.en: This word names a scale for measuring temperature. Water freezes at zero degrees and boils at one hundred degrees on this scale at normal air pressure. Many countries use it in weather reports.
The morning weather report says it is ten degrees. A coat will feel useful outside. The number is given on the common temperature scale.
A cook checks how hot an oven should be. The recipe uses degrees from this scale. It helps people compare heat.

examples.en: Capillary action draws extra-thin plastic cement into the seam, chemically welding the parts together.
examples.zh: 毛細現象將高流動性模型溜縫膠水瞬間吸入接縫，透過塑膠微熔接形成堅固結合。

examples.en: Construction workers poured fresh concrete cement into the deep foundational trenches.
examples.zh: 營建工人們俐落地將攪拌均勻的新鮮混凝土水泥，源源澆灌進深邃厚實的建築基礎溝槽中。

examples.en: A successful collaborative project helped cement a lifelong professional friendship between the two researchers.
examples.zh: 一次大獲成功的跨國科研合作專案，徹底鞏固並深化了這兩位青年學者之間終生相惜的深厚友誼。

entries.definition: 模型專用高流動性溜縫膠水；黏合

explains.en: This noun means a powder used with water and other materials to make a hard building mix. The mix can hold bricks or stones together. The word can also be a verb meaning to make a bond stronger.
A builder mixes gray powder with water and sand. The wet material is spread between bricks. It hardens as it dries.
A shared experience helps two friends trust each other more. Their bond becomes stronger over time. The verb can describe making a connection firm.

examples.en: The census showed that the town had grown.
examples.zh: 人口普查顯示這座城鎮的人口增加了。

examples.en: Every home received a census form.
examples.zh: 每戶人家都收到了一份人口普查表。

examples.en: The government uses census data to plan schools.
examples.zh: 政府利用人口普查資料規劃學校。

entries.definition: （名）人口普查；定期統計人口及其特徵的官方調查。

explains.en: This noun means an official count of people in a country or area. It often asks about age, home, and work. The results help plan public services.
A worker visits homes and asks how many people live there. The answers are recorded for the town. Officials use the count to plan schools.
A government repeats this count after several years. It can show how a population has changed. The noun names this official process.

examples.en: Taiwanese Koji ceramic art combines three-dimensional clay sculpting with vibrant, glossy low-temperature glazes.
examples.zh: 台灣傳統國寶交趾陶藝術，將生動細膩的立體泥塑與晶瑩剔透的五彩低溫軟釉完美結合。

examples.en: These exquisite ceramic wall murals have withstood seaside salt spray for over a century.
examples.zh: 這些嵌於外牆的交趾陶壁畫歷經海島鹽霧吹拂超過百年，至今依然流光溢彩。

examples.en: Ceramic relief panels illustrating mythological tales adorn the exterior walls of the shrine.
examples.zh: 一幅幅刻畫上古神仙傳奇的交趾陶立體浮雕飾板，將神龕外牆裝點得莊嚴富麗。

entries.definition: 台灣交趾陶五彩軟釉燒陶藝術的

explains.en: This adjective describes objects made from clay or similar material that is heated until hard. As a noun, it names such an object or material. Plates, tiles, and cups are common examples.
A potter shapes wet clay into a bowl and heats it in a very hot oven. The bowl becomes hard and strong. It may have a colored surface.
A kitchen floor uses hard square tiles. They can be easy to clean and last a long time. The same word describes this material.

examples.en: The agency will certify the new safety equipment.
examples.zh: 主管機關將為新安全設備核發認證。

examples.en: The teacher can certify that I completed the course.
examples.zh: 老師可以證明我已完成這門課程。

examples.en: The lab must certify each test result.
examples.zh: 實驗室必須正式確認每項檢驗結果。

entries.definition: 證明；認證；簽發證書；確認合格。

explains.en: This verb means to state officially that something is true or meets a standard. A person or group with authority usually does this. A document may serve as proof.
A trained worker checks a new machine carefully. The worker signs a paper saying it is safe to use. The paper gives official proof.
A school confirms that a student finished a course. It gives the student a document. The verb describes making that fact official.

examples.en: Please sit down on that wooden chair.
examples.zh: 請在那張木椅上坐下。

examples.en: There are not enough chairs for all the guests.
examples.zh: 沒有足夠的椅子給所有客人坐。

examples.en: He pulled out a chair and sat down next to me.
examples.zh: 他拉開一張椅子並坐在我身旁。

explains.en: These nouns can name a person who leads a meeting or group. The shorter form is often used for the role. A leader guides discussion and helps the group make decisions.
A committee meets to discuss a new plan. One person keeps the talk in order and invites each member to speak. That person leads the meeting.
A group may choose someone to guide its work for a year. The person may set meeting topics and speak for the group. The role can be held by anyone.

examples.en: They opened a bottle of champagne after the wedding.
examples.zh: 婚禮後，他們開了一瓶香檳。

examples.en: She poured champagne into small glasses.
examples.zh: 她把香檳倒進小酒杯裡。

examples.en: The team celebrated with champagne.
examples.zh: 團隊用香檳慶祝。

entries.definition: （名）香檳酒；氣泡酒；（形）淡金色的

explains.en: This noun names a sparkling wine from a region in France. People often serve it at celebrations. The drink has bubbles and is usually used for a toast.
Friends open a bottle at a wedding dinner. They pour the drink into tall glasses. The bubbles rise to the top.
A host may offer a nonalcoholic drink instead. The famous wine is closely linked with special events. Its name is also used more loosely for similar sparkling wines.

examples.en: The crowd began to chant the player’s name.
examples.zh: 群眾開始反覆喊著那位球員的名字。

examples.en: Students made up a short chant for their team.
examples.zh: 學生為自己的隊伍編了一段簡短口號。

examples.en: The workers chanted as they marched.
examples.zh: 工人們一邊遊行一邊喊著口號。

entries.definition: （名）反覆吟唱的口號；（動）吟唱；反覆呼喊

explains.en: This noun means a short set of words or sounds repeated again and again. As a verb, it means to say or sing those words in a steady rhythm. Groups often use it together.
Fans stand in the stadium and repeat the team name. Their voices follow the same beat. The repeated words encourage the players.
People walk in a group and repeat a simple line. The sound rises and falls in a regular way. The verb describes this repeated speaking.

examples.en: The charitable group raised money for families.
examples.zh: 慈善團體為家庭募款。

examples.en: She made a charitable gift to the shelter.
examples.zh: 她捐了一筆款項給收容所。

examples.en: They do charitable work in their community.
examples.zh: 他們在社區從事慈善工作。

entries.definition: （形）慈善的、樂善好施的；願意幫助有需要的人。

explains.en: This adjective describes giving help, money, or time to people in need. It can also describe an organization that supports a good cause. A generous person is willing to help others.
A family gives warm coats to a shelter in winter. The gift helps people who cannot afford them. This is an act of kindness.
A group collects money for children who need school supplies. Volunteers work without seeking payment. The adjective describes the group’s purpose.

examples.en: Regular health checkups help detect medical issues early.
examples.zh: 定期健康檢查有助於早期發現潛在醫療問題。

examples.en: I booked my annual dental checkup for next Tuesday morning.
examples.zh: 我預約了下週二早上的年度定期口腔健康檢查。

examples.en: Take your car in for a complete safety checkup before the long highway journey.
examples.zh: 在踏上長途公路旅程前，先把愛車送去做全面的安全車檢。

examples.en: Annual comprehensive health checkups detect metabolic risks and silent tumors early.
examples.zh: 養成每年定期接受全身精密健康檢查的良好習慣能及早揪出代謝異常與無痛早期腫瘤。

examples.en: Fasting for eight hours before your morning blood draw checkup is mandatory.
examples.zh: 在前往醫檢中心接受早晨空腹抽血體檢之前，前一晚午夜起嚴格禁食八小時是絕對必要的。

examples.en: Take your toddler to the pediatric clinic for regular milestone and wellness checkups.
examples.zh: 請定期帶家中幼兒前往小兒科健康門診接受各個月齡階段的生長里程碑評估與健兒體檢。

examples.en: Senior dogs benefit greatly from comprehensive bi-annual blood and ultrasound checkups.
examples.zh: 七歲以上的高齡老犬每半年定期接受一次完整的全套血液生化與腹部超音波健康檢查大有裨益。

examples.en: We scheduled a routine checkup for our rescue puppy to ensure his growth is on track.
examples.zh: 我們替剛領養的幼犬預約了例行健康檢查，確保牠的發育一切正常。

examples.en: A thorough dental checkup can detect early tartar buildup before it causes tooth loss.
examples.zh: 全面的口腔檢查能在牙結石導致掉牙前及早察覺並處理。

entries.definition: 健康檢查；體檢；全身健康檢查；例行體檢；寵物定期健康檢查

explains.en: This noun means a planned visit or inspection to see whether a person or thing is healthy and working well. A doctor may examine a person during one. A mechanic can also inspect a car this way.
A person visits a clinic once a year. The doctor asks questions and checks basic signs of health. This visit can find a problem early.
A driver takes a car to a garage before a long trip. A worker looks at the tires and brakes. The inspection helps keep the car safe.

examples.en: The chemist tested the water in the lab.
examples.zh: 化學家在實驗室檢測水質。

examples.en: She asked the chemist for cough medicine.
examples.zh: 她向藥師詢問咳嗽藥。

examples.en: A chemist studies how materials react.
examples.zh: 化學家研究物質如何產生反應。

entries.definition: 化學家；藥劑師（英式用法）。

explains.en: This noun can mean a scientist who studies substances and how they change. In some countries, it can also mean a shop that sells medicine. The setting makes the meaning clear.
A scientist mixes two safe liquids in a lab. The liquids change color. The researcher writes down what happened.
A person visits a local shop to buy medicine. A worker explains how to use it. In some places, this shop has the same name as the scientist.

examples.en: We roasted chestnuts over the fire.
examples.zh: 我們在火上烤栗子。

examples.en: A chestnut fell from the tree.
examples.zh: 一顆栗子從樹上掉下來。

examples.en: The horse had a shiny chestnut coat.
examples.zh: 那匹馬有一身亮澤的栗色毛。

explains.en: This noun names a smooth brown nut that can be cooked and eaten. It can also mean a tree that grows these nuts. The word may describe a reddish brown color.
A cook roasts a brown nut over a fire. Its shell is removed before eating. The inside is soft and mildly sweet.
A horse has a rich reddish brown coat. The color is similar to the nut’s outer shell. The adjective describes that shade.

examples.en: He added one chili to the soup.
examples.zh: 他在湯裡加了一根辣椒。

examples.en: We ate chili with rice for dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐我們吃了辣豆肉醬配飯。

examples.en: This chili is too hot for me.
examples.zh: 這種辣椒對我來說太辣了。

explains.en: This noun names a small hot pepper used to add heat to food. It can also name a spicy dish made with meat, beans, or vegetables. The spelling varies by place.
A cook cuts a red pepper and adds it to a pot. The dish becomes much hotter. Only a little may be enough.
A family serves a thick bean stew on a cold evening. It has meat and a warm spicy taste. The dish is often eaten with bread.

examples.en: A chimpanzee used a stick to reach the food.
examples.zh: 黑猩猩用樹枝取得食物。

examples.en: The young chimpanzee stayed close to its mother.
examples.zh: 年幼的黑猩猩待在母親身旁。

examples.en: Chimpanzees live in groups in the wild.
examples.zh: 黑猩猩在野外成群生活。

entries.definition: （名）黑猩猩；生活於非洲、與人類親緣相近的靈長類動物。

explains.en: This noun names a large African ape with no tail. It is intelligent and lives in groups. It can use simple tools to find food.
An animal climbs a tree and looks for fruit. It uses a small stick to reach insects. Its hands can hold objects.
A family group rests together in the forest. Young ones play while adults search for food. The animal shares many traits with humans.

examples.en: The birds chirp outside my window.
examples.zh: 鳥兒在我窗外吱吱叫。

examples.en: I heard a chirp from the smoke alarm.
examples.zh: 我聽到煙霧警報器發出一聲短促鳴響。

examples.en: A cricket chirped in the grass.
examples.zh: 一隻蟋蟀在草叢裡唧唧叫。

explains.en: This verb means to make a short, high sound like a small bird. The noun can name that sound. The sound may be repeated several times.
A small bird sits on a fence at dawn. It makes a quick, clear sound. Another bird answers from a tree.
A tiny electronic device makes a brief high note. The sound repeats when a battery is low. The noun can describe this noise too.

examples.en: Eating oat bran and leafy vegetables helps lower bad LDL cholesterol levels.
examples.zh: 多攝取燕麥麩皮與深綠色高纖蔬菜有助於顯著降低血液中壞的低密度脂蛋白膽固醇（LDL）。

examples.en: Routine annual blood tests measure total cholesterol alongside HDL and LDL readings.
examples.zh: 每年度的例行體檢抽血項目中，皆會詳細檢驗總膽固醇、高密度好膽固醇與低密度壞膽固醇。

examples.en: High cholesterol deposits can gradually narrow arteries and increase the risk of heart attacks.
examples.zh: 過多的壞膽固醇長期沉積在動脈血管內壁上，會使血管逐漸狹窄硬化並大幅增加心肌梗塞風險。

explains.en: This noun names a waxy substance in the blood and body. The body needs some, but too much of certain kinds can harm the heart and blood vessels. A blood test can measure its level.
A person has a routine blood test at a clinic. The report gives a number for a fatty substance in the blood. The doctor can explain what the number means.
Food and family history can affect the amount in the body. A health worker may suggest changes after reviewing test results. The substance is linked to heart health.

examples.en: He put the cigar back in its case.
examples.zh: 他把雪茄放回盒子裡。

examples.en: The cigar had a strong smell.
examples.zh: 那支雪茄氣味很濃。

examples.en: A cigar is made from rolled tobacco leaves.
examples.zh: 雪茄是用捲起來的菸葉製成的。

entries.definition: （名）雪茄；捲成柱狀的菸草製品

explains.en: This noun means a roll of dried tobacco leaves that people smoke. It is usually larger than a cigarette. It can have a strong smell.
A person takes a long brown roll from a box. It is made from tobacco leaves. Smoke comes from its end when lit.
Some people use this item to celebrate a special event. It may be sold in a small shop. Smoking it can harm health.

examples.en: The new roads helped civilize the remote region.
examples.zh: 新道路促進了偏遠地區的城鎮發展。

examples.en: A quiet meal helped civilize the noisy meeting.
examples.zh: 一頓安靜的餐點讓吵鬧的聚會變得有禮貌。

examples.en: Some writers used the word to civilize other societies.
examples.zh: 有些作家用這個詞描述讓其他社會採用城鎮生活方式。

explains.en: This verb means to change a place or society by building towns and introducing new ways of life. It can also mean to make behavior more polite. The word can sound judgmental when used about cultures.
People build roads, homes, and schools in a growing area. Daily life changes as more people settle there. The verb describes this kind of change.
A host asks guests to speak kindly and wait their turn. Their behavior becomes more polite. The verb can describe making conduct more respectful.

examples.en: We ordered clam soup at the seaside cafe.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊咖啡館點了蛤蜊湯。

examples.en: A clam was buried in the wet sand.
examples.zh: 一隻蛤蜊埋在濕沙裡。

examples.en: The cook steamed clams with garlic.
examples.zh: 廚師用大蒜蒸蛤蜊。

explains.en: This noun names a sea animal with a soft body inside two hard shells. People often cook and eat it. It lives in sand or mud under the water.
A cook opens a shell and removes the soft meat inside. It goes into a pot with soup. The animal came from the sea.
At low tide, someone finds a pair of shells buried in wet sand. They close tightly when touched. The animal lives inside them.

examples.en: She clasped her hands before the speech.
examples.zh: 演講前，她緊握雙手。

examples.en: The necklace clasp was broken.
examples.zh: 項鍊的扣環壞了。

examples.en: He clasped the warm cup with both hands.
examples.zh: 他雙手緊握著溫熱的杯子。

explains.en: This verb means to hold something tightly with the hands or arms. As a noun, it means a small fastener that joins two parts. It can keep a necklace, bag, or belt closed.
A child holds a parent’s hand during a busy crossing. The grip is firm. The verb describes holding on closely.
A small metal part clicks shut on a necklace. It keeps the two ends together. The noun names this fastener.

examples.en: The crew began clearance of the blocked road.
examples.zh: 工作人員開始清理被堵住的道路。

examples.en: You need security clearance to enter this room.
examples.zh: 你需要安全許可才能進入這個房間。

examples.en: The store put winter coats on clearance.
examples.zh: 商店把冬季外套列入清倉特價。

explains.en: This noun can mean the act of removing things from a space. It can also mean official permission to enter or use something. In a shop, it can refer to goods sold at lower prices to make room.
Workers move boxes out of a hallway. The open path lets people pass safely. The noun names the removal of objects.
A visitor gets approval before entering a secure room. A shop may also lower prices on older goods. The same word has these different uses.

examples.en: The climax of the film surprised everyone.
examples.zh: 電影的高潮讓所有人都感到意外。

examples.en: The story builds slowly and then climaxes at the final scene.
examples.zh: 故事慢慢鋪陳，接著在最後一幕達到高潮。

examples.en: Their argument reached a climax near midnight.
examples.zh: 他們的爭論在午夜前後達到最激烈的時刻。

explains.en: This noun means the most exciting or important point in a story or event. It often comes near the end. As a verb, it means to reach that high point.
A mystery story reveals who took the missing jewels. The reader has waited for this answer. This moment is the most exciting part.
A long race reaches its final lap. The runners are close together and the crowd shouts. The event reaches its highest point.

examples.en: Turn the lid clockwise to close the jar.
examples.zh: 順時針轉動瓶蓋，把罐子蓋緊。

examples.en: The wheel moves clockwise in this picture.
examples.zh: 圖中的輪子順時針轉動。

examples.en: Make a clockwise turn at the next street.
examples.zh: 在下一條街順時針方向轉彎。

entries.definition: （副／形）順時針方向地（的）；沿鐘面指針方向移動。

explains.en: This word describes a direction that follows the hands of a clock. It can be used as an adverb or adjective. The opposite direction goes the other way around.
A person turns a round handle toward the right. The movement follows the usual path of clock hands. The word describes this direction.
A diagram shows an arrow circling a center point. The arrow moves from top to right, then down. This is the direction named by the word.

examples.en: Scientists cloned the plant from a small cutting.
examples.zh: 科學家用一小段枝條複製了這株植物。

examples.en: The lab grew a clone of the original cell.
examples.zh: 實驗室培養出原始細胞的複製體。

examples.en: He cloned the old computer drive onto a new one.
examples.zh: 他把舊電腦硬碟完整複製到新硬碟。

explains.en: This noun means a living thing or cell that is copied from another with the same genes. As a verb, it means to make such a copy. The word is also used for an exact copy of a computer program or object.
A plant grows from a cutting taken from another plant. The new plant has the same genetic information. It is a copy of the first one.
A technician makes a copy of a computer drive. The files and setup are almost the same. The verb can describe making this kind of copy.

examples.en: Solving the cold case forty years later brought long-awaited closure and peace to the grieving family.
examples.zh: 在事隔四十年後終於宣告破案逮捕真兇，為長期承受巨大悲痛的被害者家屬帶來期盼已久的心靈釋懷。

examples.en: Finding the missing child’s remains finally allowed parents to experience painful closure.
examples.zh: 歷經漫長歲月終於尋獲失蹤愛子的遺骸，終於讓白髮蒼蒼的父母親在傷痛中得到了最終的心靈平息。

examples.en: Bringing the fugitive to trial provides the surviving community with a vital sense of legal and emotional closure.
examples.zh: 將逃亡多年的要犯正式逮捕緝拿歸案受審，為劫後餘生的社區居民帶來了法律與情感上的深層釋懷與平靜。

entries.definition: 破案告慰受害者家屬帶來心靈終結平靜

explains.en: This noun means a feeling that an event has been settled or brought to an end. It is often used after a painful loss or a long problem. A clear answer may help someone move forward.
A family learns what happened to a missing loved one. The news is painful, but they can stop waiting. They feel a sense of peace.
A worker finishes a difficult project and turns in the last report. The task is complete. The person can now focus on something new.

examples.en: The parties formed a coalition after the election.
examples.zh: 選舉後，這些政黨組成了聯盟。

examples.en: A coalition of local groups cleaned the beach.
examples.zh: 地方團體組成的聯盟清理了海灘。

examples.en: The coalition agreed on a shared plan.
examples.zh: 這個聯盟同意了一項共同計畫。

explains.en: This noun means a group of people or organizations that join for a shared purpose. The members may keep their own identities. They work together on a goal or issue.
Several small groups join to clean a river. Each group brings its own volunteers. Together they can do more work.
Political parties may join to form a government. They agree to cooperate despite some differences. The noun names this kind of group.

examples.en: Taiwan features more than 1,500 kilometers of diverse scenic coastline.
examples.zh: 台灣擁有超過一千五百公里風貌多樣的迷人海岸線。

examples.en: Taking Provincial Highway 11 offers panoramic views of the rugged eastern coastline.
examples.zh: 沿著台十一線省道行駛，能將壯麗險峻的東部海岸線全景盡收眼底。

examples.en: Coastal erosion threatens sandy beaches along certain stretches of the western coastline.
examples.zh: 海岸侵蝕現象對西部海岸線某些區段的細緻沙灘造成了嚴重的流失威脅。

explains.en: This noun means the line where land meets the sea. It may be smooth or have many bays and cliffs. Maps show it along the edge of a country or island.
A family walks beside the water and follows the edge of the land. The path curves around a bay. It marks the border between sea and land.
A storm changes some beaches over time. Maps may show where the shore bends. The noun describes this outline.

examples.en: Automatic emergency braking prevented a serious rear-end highway collision.
examples.zh: 前方主動防撞緊急煞車系統（AEB）成功化解了一起險些發生的國道追撞事故。

examples.en: The intersection collision caused major morning gridlock across three city lanes.
examples.zh: 十字路口發生的兩車碰撞車禍導致市區三個主要車道在早尖峰陷入嚴重回堵。

examples.en: Modern crumple zones absorb kinetic impact energy during a frontal collision.
examples.zh: 現代汽車的車頭潰縮防護區能在正面猛烈衝撞時吸收衝擊動能，保護座艙完整。

explains.en: This noun means an event in which two moving things hit each other. It often refers to cars, bikes, or objects in space. It can cause damage or injury.
Two cars reach an intersection at the same time and hit. One has a broken door. The crash blocks the road.
A ball strikes a window while flying through the air. The glass breaks on impact. The noun can describe this sudden hit.

examples.en: The word is colloquial and common in daily speech.
examples.zh: 這個字屬於口語，常見於日常交談。

examples.en: Her essay avoids colloquial expressions.
examples.zh: 她的文章避免使用口語表達。

examples.en: This phrase sounds colloquial to many readers.
examples.zh: 許多讀者覺得這個片語聽起來很口語。

explains.en: This adjective describes words and phrases used in relaxed everyday speech. Such language may be common among friends but unsuitable for formal writing. It can vary by place or group.
Two friends talk using short, familiar phrases. They do not speak like a news report. Their language is casual.
A student writes an essay for a teacher. The student chooses more formal words. The adjective describes the relaxed words often heard in conversation.

examples.en: Halley's Comet visits our inner solar system once every seventy-six years.
examples.zh: 鼎鼎大名的哈雷彗星每隔約七十六年便會造訪一次內太陽系軌道。

examples.en: As a frozen comet nears the Sun, solar radiation vaporizes its ice, forming a spectacular glowing tail.
examples.zh: 當由冰雪與岩屑構成的彗星接近太陽時，強烈太陽輻射蒸發其冰層，在身後拖曳出一道壯麗璀璨的彗尾。

examples.en: Ancient superstition often regarded the sudden appearance of a bright comet as an omen of change.
examples.zh: 遠古古代文明往往出於迷信，將夜空中突兀現身的明亮掃帚星彗星視為王朝更迭或天下大亂的凶兆。

examples.en: Sunlight vaporizes a comet's icy core, blowing a glowing dust and ion tail millions of miles long.
examples.zh: 當彗星接近太陽時，強烈陽光蒸發其冰雪核，在太空中拉出一條長達數百萬公里的璀璨離子彗尾。

examples.en: Halley's Comet is visible from Earth with the naked eye once every seventy-six years.
examples.zh: 舉世聞名的哈雷彗星（Halley's Comet）每隔大約七十六年便會繞行接近地球一次，肉眼即可清晰仰望。

examples.en: Scientists believe comets may have delivered water and primordial organic building blocks to young Earth.
examples.zh: 許多天體物理學家深信，在遠古時代密集撞擊地球的彗星，很可能為剛誕生的原始地球帶來了豐沛的水源與有機分子。

entries.definition: 彗星；掃帚星；彗星（掃帚星）；冰雪天體

explains.en: This noun names an object in space made mostly of ice and dust. It moves around the sun in a long path. When it comes near the sun, gas and dust can form a bright tail.
People watch the night sky as a bright object moves across it. A pale tail follows behind. It can be seen for a short time.
The object travels far from the sun and returns after many years. Some have paths that take a very long time. The noun names this space object.

examples.en: Online meetings have become commonplace.
examples.zh: 線上會議已變得很普遍。

examples.en: It is commonplace to use a phone for directions.
examples.zh: 用手機導航是很常見的事。

examples.en: The saying is a commonplace in many books.
examples.zh: 這句格言在許多書中都很常見。

entries.definition: （形）平凡的、常見的；（名）老生常談、陳腔濫調。

explains.en: This adjective describes something ordinary and seen often. As a noun, it can mean a familiar idea or saying. The word suggests that something is no longer surprising.
Many people carry a phone with a camera. This is normal in daily life now. The adjective describes something usual.
A writer repeats a familiar saying about hard work. Readers have heard it many times. The noun can name such a common idea.

examples.en: The commonwealth has its own local government.
examples.zh: 這個自治政體有自己的地方政府。

examples.en: She studied the history of the Commonwealth of Australia.
examples.zh: 她研究了澳大利亞聯邦的歷史。

examples.en: The commonwealth held a public vote.
examples.zh: 這個自治政體舉行了公投。

entries.definition: 聯邦；共和國；共同體；公共利益。

explains.en: This noun can mean a political community or a state that governs itself. It is also part of the official name of some countries or regions. The exact meaning depends on the place.
A group of people shares laws and public services. The community has its own government. The noun can describe this political body.
A traveler reads the formal name of a region on a map. It includes this word as part of its title. In that case, it is an official name.

examples.en: He is friendly and communicative with his coworkers.
examples.zh: 他對同事友善，也樂於溝通。

examples.en: The teacher used a communicative activity in class.
examples.zh: 老師在課堂上使用了溝通式活動。

examples.en: A communicative child often shares ideas with others.
examples.zh: 善於溝通的孩子常和別人分享想法。

entries.definition: （形）健談的；善於溝通的；傳達訊息的

explains.en: This adjective describes someone who shares thoughts and information clearly. It can also describe something that helps people exchange messages. Listening and speaking are both part of good communication.
A new student asks questions and tells classmates about her ideas. Others understand what she needs. She is open in conversation.
A phone app lets family members send short messages. People can share news from far away. The adjective can describe tools that support this exchange.

examples.en: The study made a comparative review of the two plans.
examples.zh: 這項研究對兩個計畫進行了比較。

examples.en: “Better” is the comparative form of “good.”
examples.zh: 「Better」是「good」的比較級形式。

examples.en: The comparative report found that Plan A cost less.
examples.zh: 比較報告發現A計畫的費用較低。

explains.en: This adjective means involving a comparison between things. In grammar, it describes a form used to compare two people or objects. It can also mean fairly good when compared with another choice.
A report looks at the cost of two plans side by side. It points out what is cheaper. The report makes a comparison.
The word “smaller” compares two sizes. It has a different form from the basic adjective. This grammatical term describes that form.

examples.en: The compass pointed north on the trail.
examples.zh: 在步道上，指南針指向北方。

examples.en: She used a compass to find the campsite.
examples.zh: 她用指南針找到露營地。

examples.en: A compass can help sailors at sea.
examples.zh: 指南針能幫助水手在海上辨認方向。

explains.en: This noun names a tool that shows direction. A magnetic needle points north and helps people find their way. It can be used on land or at sea.
A hiker checks a small tool before choosing a trail. Its needle points toward north. The map and needle help guide the walk.
A ship travels far from shore with no roads nearby. The crew checks direction as they move. The tool helps them stay on course.

examples.en: She compiled a list of useful websites.
examples.zh: 她整理了一份實用網站清單。

examples.en: The editor compiled the letters into a book.
examples.zh: 編輯把這些信件編成一本書。

examples.en: The program will compile the code tonight.
examples.zh: 程式今晚會編譯這段程式碼。

explains.en: This verb means to collect information or items and put them together in one place. It can also mean to turn computer instructions into a form a machine can run. The purpose is to make a complete set.
A student gathers facts from books and notes. The student arranges them into a report. The verb describes putting the information together.
A computer program is changed into a form that a machine can use. A tool checks the instructions and creates a working file. This is another use of the verb.

examples.en: The sauce complements the grilled fish.
examples.zh: 這種醬汁很適合搭配烤魚。

examples.en: A small side dish is a nice complement to the meal.
examples.zh: 一道小菜是這餐很好的搭配。

examples.en: Her skills complement the rest of the team.
examples.zh: 她的技能補足了團隊其他成員的長處。

entries.definition: （名）補充物；互補部分；（動）補足；使更完整

explains.en: This noun means something that completes or improves another thing. As a verb, it means to go well with something. It adds what is missing or makes a good match.
A meal has soup, bread, and a fresh salad. Each part works well with the others. The salad completes the meal.
A blue scarf looks good with a gray coat. The colors suit each other. The verb describes how one thing improves the other.

examples.en: The cold weather made her complexion look pale.
examples.zh: 寒冷的天氣讓她的氣色看起來蒼白。

examples.en: The new rule changed the complexion of the debate.
examples.zh: 新規定改變了這場辯論的整體面貌。

examples.en: He has a clear complexion.
examples.zh: 他的膚色看起來很健康。

explains.en: This noun means the natural color and appearance of a person’s facial skin. It can also mean the general nature of a situation. The second meaning is more formal.
A person looks in a mirror after a long walk in the sun. The face is red and warm. The noun describes the skin’s appearance.
A town changes after a large factory opens. The local economy now looks different. The word can describe the overall character of a situation.

examples.en: The book gives a comprehensive guide to local birds.
examples.zh: 這本書完整介紹了當地的鳥類。

examples.en: The report offers a comprehensive review of the plan.
examples.zh: 這份報告全面檢視了這項計畫。

examples.en: We need a comprehensive list of all costs.
examples.zh: 我們需要一份涵蓋所有費用的完整清單。

entries.definition: （形）全面的、完整的；涵蓋多數重要部分的。

explains.en: This adjective describes something that covers many parts or details. It aims to include everything important. A complete guide or review may have this quality.
A guide explains how to apply, what papers to bring, and when to expect an answer. It covers each step. Readers can find most needed details in one place.
A doctor reviews a person’s health, habits, and test results. The review looks at many parts together. The adjective describes its wide coverage.

examples.en: Massive supercomputing compute clusters are the lifeblood required to train trillion-parameter frontier models.
examples.zh: 由數萬張頂級晶片組成的巨型高效能算力叢集（Compute），是訓練兆級參數前沿旗艦大模型的必備基石。

examples.en: Researchers submitted a formal proposal requesting access to national supercomputing compute cycles for drug discovery.
examples.zh: 國家衛生研究院生醫研發團隊正式遞交專案計畫，申請使用國家級高速超級電腦中心的龐大算力資源進行新藥合成。

examples.en: As artificial neural networks scale up, access to affordable clean energy and scalable compute determines AI leadership.
examples.zh: 隨著深度神經網絡規模持續指數級膨脹，能否取得充沛廉價的綠色電能與可彈性擴充的高效算力將決定科技話語權。

entries.definition: 國家級超級 AI 龐大算力資源；計算

explains.en: This verb means to work out a number or answer using math or a machine. A computer can process information by following steps. The word is often used in technical settings.
A worker adds the prices of several items. A small machine gives the total. The verb describes working out the number.
A large machine handles many pieces of information at once. It follows instructions and produces an answer. This is another use of the verb.

examples.en: The school plans to computerize its old records.
examples.zh: 學校計畫將舊紀錄電腦化。

examples.en: The company computerized its payment system.
examples.zh: 公司把付款系統改成電腦化作業。

examples.en: They computerize each new library book.
examples.zh: 他們把每本新進館藏登錄到電腦系統。

entries.definition: 使電腦化；用電腦處理或控制。

explains.en: This verb means to change a task or record so that a computer handles it. It may replace paper files or manual steps. The change can make searching and updating easier.
A library enters its books into a digital system. Staff can search titles on a screen. The work has moved from paper to computers.
A small shop keeps sales records by hand. It begins using software instead. The verb describes making this change.

examples.en: He thanked his comrades for their support.
examples.zh: 他感謝同伴們的支持。

examples.en: A comrade helped her carry the supplies.
examples.zh: 一位夥伴幫她搬運物資。

examples.en: The soldiers stood beside their comrades.
examples.zh: 士兵們站在同袍身旁。

explains.en: This noun means a companion who shares work, danger, or a cause with another person. It can refer to a fellow soldier or a close companion in a group. The tone may sound formal or old-fashioned.
Two workers face a difficult task together. They help each other and trust one another. Each is a close companion to the other.
A soldier remembers people who served in the same unit. They shared danger and daily life. The noun can describe such a fellow member.

examples.en: The software vendor made price concessions in exchange for multi-year contracts.
examples.zh: 軟體原廠給予了價格上的折扣讓步，以換取簽署為期數年的長期合約。

examples.en: Neither party was willing to make a concession regarding delivery deadlines.
examples.zh: 雙方都不願意在交貨截止日期上做出任何妥協退讓。

examples.en: The government granted the company a twenty-year mining concession.
examples.zh: 政府授予該公司長達二十年的礦產開採特許權。

explains.en: This noun means something given up or allowed to reach an agreement. It can also mean a special right granted by an authority. At a theater or stadium, it may name a place selling snacks.
Two neighbors disagree about a fence. One agrees to move it a little. This small change helps them settle the argument.
A worker buys popcorn from a counter at a game. A company has permission to sell food there. The noun can refer to that permission or place.

examples.en: Please keep your report concise and clear.
examples.zh: 請讓報告簡潔明瞭。

examples.en: Her concise note explained the change.
examples.zh: 她簡短的便條說明了這項變更。

examples.en: The guide gives concise directions to the station.
examples.zh: 這份指南簡潔地說明了前往車站的路線。

explains.en: This adjective describes speech or writing that uses few words while giving the needed information. It avoids extra detail. A short message can still be clear.
A sign says “Keep door closed” instead of using a long note. People understand the request quickly. The message is brief and clear.
A student answers a question in two direct sentences. The answer includes the key point without extra words. The adjective describes this style.

examples.en: The editor condensed the report to one page.
examples.zh: 編輯把報告縮短成一頁。

examples.en: Steam can condense on a cold surface.
examples.zh: 蒸氣可能在冰冷表面凝結。

examples.en: Please condense your answer into two sentences.
examples.zh: 請把答案濃縮成兩個句子。

entries.definition: （動）濃縮、凝結；縮短內容或使氣體變成液體。

explains.en: This verb means to make something shorter or smaller while keeping the main information. It can also mean to change a gas into liquid. The context shows which meaning is intended.
A long article is cut down to a few key points. The reader can finish it quickly. The writer has made the text shorter.
Warm water vapor touches a cold window and turns into drops. The change forms liquid from gas. The verb names this change.

examples.en: The confederation brought several regions together.
examples.zh: 這個邦聯把數個地區聯合起來。

examples.en: Each member of the confederation kept local control.
examples.zh: 邦聯的每個成員都保留地方自治權。

examples.en: The clubs formed a confederation for the tournament.
examples.zh: 這些俱樂部為了賽事組成聯合組織。

entries.definition: 聯邦；邦聯；結盟；聯盟組織。

explains.en: This noun means a union of states or groups that keep some power for themselves. They join to cooperate on certain matters. The central group may have limited control.
Several regions agree to share defense and trade. Each region still makes many local rules. Their union is a political partnership.
Different sports clubs join an organization to set shared rules. Each club remains separate. The noun can describe this kind of union.

examples.en: The congressman spoke about the new bill.
examples.zh: 這位男性國會議員談到了新法案。

examples.en: The congressman answered questions after the vote.
examples.zh: 投票後，這位國會議員回答了問題。

examples.en: The veteran congressman sponsored an agricultural bipartisan relief bill to support family farms.
examples.zh: 這位資深國會議員發起了一項兩黨聯合支持的農業紓困救助法案，以支持家庭農場。

entries.definition: （名）國會議員；美國眾議院議員

explains.en: These nouns name a person elected to serve in a national lawmaking body. One form refers to a man and another to a woman. The shorter gender-neutral title is often used today.
Voters choose a local representative to speak for them in the capital. The person helps discuss and pass laws. The role is filled through an election.
A person writes to an elected lawmaker about a new bill. The official reads concerns from people in the district. The title names this kind of representative.

examples.en: The conquest changed the map of the region.
examples.zh: 這場征服改變了該地區的版圖。

examples.en: The team celebrated its conquest of the mountain.
examples.zh: 隊伍慶祝成功征服那座山。

examples.en: The conquest of the island took many years.
examples.zh: 征服這座島花了很多年。

explains.en: This noun means taking control of a place or people by force. It can also mean a difficult success achieved through effort. The word is often used in history.
An army enters a city and takes power after a battle. The people lose control of their land. The event changes who rules the area.
A climber reaches a very high peak after years of training. It was a hard goal to achieve. The noun can describe this success.

examples.en: She is a conscientious nurse who checks every detail.
examples.zh: 她是一位做事細心、會檢查每個細節的護理師。

examples.en: A conscientious student turns in work on time.
examples.zh: 認真的學生會準時交作業。

examples.en: He made a conscientious effort to help.
examples.zh: 他盡責地努力提供協助。

entries.definition: （形）認真盡責的；細心而努力地做好應負責的事。

explains.en: This adjective describes someone who takes care to do work well and responsibly. Such a person notices details and tries to meet duties. The word often praises careful behavior.
A worker checks each number before sending a bill. The worker does not rush through the task. This shows care and responsibility.
A student finishes assignments on time and follows the instructions. The student wants the work to be accurate. The adjective describes this careful attitude.

examples.en: We should conserve water during the dry season.
examples.zh: 乾旱季節我們應該節約用水。

examples.en: The group works to conserve the forest.
examples.zh: 這個團體致力於保護森林。

examples.en: A lid can help conserve heat in the pot.
examples.zh: 蓋上鍋蓋有助於保存鍋中的熱度。

explains.en: This verb means to protect something and use it carefully so it lasts. It often refers to water, energy, or nature. It can also mean to keep food from being wasted.
A family turns off lights when leaving a room. They use less electricity. The verb describes saving a resource.
Workers protect a wetland so birds can keep living there. They prevent damage to the land. This use means taking care of nature.

examples.en: Her kind words were a consolation after the loss.
examples.zh: 失敗後，她的安慰話語帶來了一些慰藉。

examples.en: The small prize offered little consolation.
examples.zh: 這個小獎項只能帶來些許安慰。

examples.en: He found consolation in the support of friends.
examples.zh: 他從朋友的支持中得到慰藉。

entries.definition: （名）安慰；慰藉；令人寬慰的事物

explains.en: This noun means comfort given to someone who feels sad or disappointed. It may come from kind words or a small reward. It does not always remove the sadness.
A child loses a game and begins to cry. A parent sits nearby and speaks gently. The comfort helps the child feel less alone.
A team misses the final but receives a prize for fair play. The award is not the main victory. It gives some comfort after the loss.

examples.en: Next-gen home gaming consoles support 4K 120Hz high-definition gaming.
examples.zh: 次世代頂級家用遊戲主機全面支援 4K 120Hz 超高畫質與極速固態硬碟秒速載入。

examples.en: Families often gather in the living room to play party games together on the TV console.
examples.zh: 全家人每逢週末最愛聚在客廳大螢幕電視前，連上遊戲主機一起暢玩派對同樂遊戲。

examples.en: The technician checked the control console to diagnose the electrical system fault.
examples.zh: 維修工程技師仔細檢查中控操作控制台上的各項監控數據，以診斷電力系統的跳電異常。

examples.en: Sitting comfortably at the ergonomic console, the surgeon views high-definition 3D magnified anatomical structures.
examples.zh: 主刀醫師端坐於符合人體工學的控制台（Console）前，透過 3D 高畫質放大目鏡清晰透視體內微細解剖構造。

examples.en: Teenagers connected their favorite gaming console to the living room television for a weekend tournament.
examples.zh: 國高中青年在週末將最新款次世代家庭電視遊戲主機連接至客廳大螢幕，與好友熱血展開雙打電競對決。

examples.en: She struggled to console her weeping best friend after the sudden passing of her golden retriever.
examples.zh: 面對陪伴十年的愛犬黃金獵犬突然安詳離世，她坐在沙發旁溫柔擁抱並竭盡全力撫慰（Console）泣不成聲的摯友。

entries.definition: 家用遊戲主機；掌上型主機；控制台；主刀醫師遠端操作控制台

explains.en: This noun can mean a control panel with switches or screens. It can also mean a home video game device. As a verb, it means to comfort someone who is sad.
A worker sits before a panel and watches several screens. Buttons control machines in a room. The noun names this control station.
A family connects a game device to the television. Players use handheld controls to play. The noun also names this home system.

examples.en: The word “sun” begins with a consonant.
examples.zh: 「sun」這個字以子音開頭。

examples.en: B is a consonant in English.
examples.zh: B 是英文中的子音字母。

examples.en: The final consonant is hard to hear.
examples.zh: 最後的子音很難聽清楚。

explains.en: This noun names a speech sound made by partly or fully blocking the flow of air. It also names a letter that usually represents such a sound. In English, most letters are in this group.
A child says the sound at the start of “cat.” The tongue briefly blocks the air. The sound is different from a vowel.
A word has letters such as B, T, and M. These are not A, E, I, O, or U. The noun can refer to these letters.

examples.en: The police uncovered a conspiracy to steal public funds.
examples.zh: 警方揭發了一項竊取公款的陰謀。

examples.en: They were accused of joining a conspiracy.
examples.zh: 他們被指控參與陰謀。

examples.en: The novel centers on a political conspiracy.
examples.zh: 這本小說以一場政治陰謀為核心。

entries.definition: （名）陰謀、密謀；多人秘密計畫做不法或有害之事。

explains.en: This noun means a secret plan made by two or more people to do something harmful or illegal. The plan is usually hidden from others. It may be discussed in law or stories.
Several people secretly plan to steal money from their company. They hide their talks from coworkers. Their secret plan breaks the law.
A mystery story hints that leaders are working together in secret. The reader slowly learns what they intend to do. The noun names such a hidden plan.

examples.en: The main contention was about the cost of the plan.
examples.zh: 主要爭議在於計畫的費用。

examples.en: Their contention lasted through the meeting.
examples.zh: 他們的爭論持續了整場會議。

examples.en: She rejected his contention that the road was safe.
examples.zh: 她不接受他所主張的道路安全說法。

explains.en: This noun means a strong disagreement or argument between people. It can also mean a point that someone argues is true. The context shows whether it is a dispute or a claim.
Two neighbors argue about where a fence should go. Neither agrees with the other. Their disagreement continues for weeks.
A writer says that the new rule will save money. Another person questions this idea. The word can name the point being argued.

examples.en: Each contestant received a number before the race.
examples.zh: 每位參賽者在比賽前都拿到一個號碼。

examples.en: The final contestant answered the last question.
examples.zh: 最後一位參賽者回答了最後一個問題。

examples.en: Contestants must follow the same rules.
examples.zh: 參賽者必須遵守相同規則。

explains.en: This noun means a person who takes part in a contest or competition. People may compete for a prize, title, or chance to win. Each person follows the same rules.
Several people answer questions on a television show. The person with the most correct answers may win. Each player is taking part in the game.
Runners line up before a race begins. They hope to finish first. The noun names each person in the competition.

examples.en: Passing ancestral traditions down to our children guarantees cultural continuity through the centuries.
examples.zh: 將先民智慧、歲時節慶與神明信仰一代代傳承給下一代，確保了島嶼文明數百年來延綿不絕的延續性。

examples.en: The revival of ancient temple festivals creates a vital bridge of historical continuity for modern youth.
examples.zh: 百年迎神祭典的風華再現，為當代年輕人搭建起一座跨越世代的歷史文化延續性橋樑。

examples.en: In times of rapid urbanization, maintaining architectural continuity keeps city memories intact.
examples.zh: 在都會急速擴張的浪潮中，保持歷史建築的脈絡延續性，才能讓城市的集體靈魂記憶完好長存。

entries.definition: 跨越數百年延綿不絕之文化延續性

explains.en: This noun means a state in which something continues without a major break or change. It can describe a story, service, or tradition. A steady link connects one part to the next.
A village keeps the same yearly festival for many generations. Families teach its customs to their children. The tradition carries on over time.
A hospital keeps its service running during a move. Patients can still receive care. The noun describes this steady connection.

examples.en: The witness did not contradict her earlier statement.
examples.zh: 證人沒有否認自己先前的說法。

examples.en: His actions contradict what he said.
examples.zh: 他的行為和他說的話相矛盾。

examples.en: The two reports contradict each other.
examples.zh: 這兩份報告彼此矛盾。

explains.en: This verb means to say that a statement is wrong or untrue. It can also mean that two facts cannot both be true. The ideas directly oppose each other.
One witness says the car was blue. Another says it was red. The second account disagrees with the first.
A sign says the store opens at nine, but its website says ten. The two pieces of information cannot both be right. The verb describes this conflict.

examples.en: The committee will convene next week.
examples.zh: 委員會將於下週開會。

examples.en: The mayor convened a meeting about road safety.
examples.zh: 市長召集了一場討論道路安全的會議。

examples.en: The judges convened to review the case.
examples.zh: 評審們聚集起來審查案件。

entries.definition: （動）召集、召開；安排人們聚集開會。

explains.en: This verb means to bring people together for a meeting. It may also mean that a group gathers on its own. The meeting is often planned and has a purpose.
The school principal asks teachers to meet on Monday. They gather in one room to discuss schedules. The verb describes calling the meeting.
A committee gathers to review a new plan. Members sit down and begin their work. The verb can describe their coming together.

examples.en: Scleractinian stony corals construct massive calcium carbonate skeletons that form living underwater reefs.
examples.zh: 造礁「石珊瑚」（Stony Corals）分泌碳酸鈣骨骼，在漫長歲月中構築成萬千生物棲息的活體珊瑚礁。

examples.en: Snorkelers floated quietly above the shallow bay to admire vibrant colonies of staghorn coral.
examples.zh: 浮潛遊客靜靜漂浮在平靜的淺水灣水面上，由衷讚嘆水底生機勃勃、宛如鹿角般的繁茂珊瑚群。

examples.en: Ocean acidification threatens delicate coral polyps by dissolving their mineralized calcium protective homes.
examples.zh: 全球海洋酸化危機溶解了碳酸鈣礦物結構，正嚴重威脅著嬌弱珊瑚蟲用以遮風避雨的堅硬鈣質家園。

entries.definition: 嬌貴造礁石珊瑚 (如鹿角珊瑚與腦紋珊瑚)

explains.en: This noun names a hard sea material made by tiny animals living together. It often forms reefs in warm, shallow water. The word can also describe a pink-orange color.
A diver sees a large structure under the sea. Many tiny animals built it over a long time. Fish swim around it.
A shirt has a soft pink-orange shade. The color resembles some sea growth. The same noun can name this color.

examples.en: The detectives found a corpse near the river.
examples.zh: 偵探在河邊發現一具屍體。

examples.en: The novel begins when a corpse is discovered.
examples.zh: 這本小說從發現一具屍體開始。

examples.en: The corpse was taken to the hospital for an examination.
examples.zh: 屍體被送到醫院進行檢查。

explains.en: This noun means the body of a dead person or animal. It is most often used in serious or formal situations. News and crime stories may use it.
Police find a dead body after a crime. They keep the area closed while they investigate. The noun names the body.
A large animal dies in the forest. Other animals may come near it. The same word can refer to a dead animal’s body.

examples.en: Their correspondence continued for many years.
examples.zh: 他們的通信持續了許多年。

examples.en: The file contains correspondence between the two offices.
examples.zh: 檔案裡有兩個辦公室之間的往來信件。

examples.en: There is a close correspondence between the map and the road.
examples.zh: 地圖和道路之間高度吻合。

entries.definition: （名）通信往來；書信；相符；對應關係

explains.en: This noun means letters or messages exchanged between people. It can also mean a close match between two things. The word often sounds formal.
A student writes to a pen pal in another country. They send letters to each other every month. Their written messages form an exchange.
A map shows a line that matches a road on the ground. The two lines agree closely. The noun can describe this match.

examples.en: She made a cosmetic change to the room.
examples.zh: 她稍微改變了房間的外觀。

examples.en: The doctor explained the cosmetic procedure.
examples.zh: 醫師說明了這項美容療程。

examples.en: He bought a cosmetic to cover a small mark.
examples.zh: 他買了一件化妝品來遮住小斑點。

explains.en: This adjective describes something used to improve appearance rather than treat a serious problem. It can also describe a small change that affects how something looks. As a noun, it can mean a beauty product.
A person uses cream to make skin look smoother. It changes the appearance for a while. It does not cure an illness.
A company changes the color of its website but keeps its services the same. The change is only about how it looks. The adjective describes this kind of change.

examples.en: The store sells cosmetics from many brands.
examples.zh: 這家商店販售許多品牌的化妝品。

examples.en: She packed her cosmetics in a small bag.
examples.zh: 她把化妝品裝進一個小包裡。

examples.en: Some cosmetics are made for sensitive skin.
examples.zh: 有些化妝品是為敏感肌膚設計的。

entries.definition: （名）化妝品；用於清潔、保養或改變外貌的產品。

explains.en: This plural noun means products used to improve or change the appearance of the face or body. It includes items such as lipstick and face powder. People choose them for different reasons.
A person puts colored cream on the lips before going out. Another uses powder to reduce shine. These products are sold in a beauty shop.
A store keeps brushes, eye color, and skin products on one shelf. Customers can test some items. The plural noun names this group of products.

examples.en: The manager spoke with her counterpart in the other office.
examples.zh: 經理和另一間辦公室的同職位主管交談。

examples.en: The local law has no exact counterpart abroad.
examples.zh: 國外沒有完全對應的當地法律。

examples.en: He met his counterpart at the conference.
examples.zh: 他在會議上見到了職務相同的人。

entries.definition: 對應的人或物；相當物；對方。

explains.en: This noun means a person or thing with the same role in another place or group. It can also mean something that matches another item. The two sides are similar in function.
A teacher visits a school in another city. She meets the teacher who has the same job there. The two workers share a role.
A phone model has a matching version made by another company. The products serve the same purpose. The noun can name the matching item.

examples.en: You can redeem this electronic discount coupon on your app.
examples.zh: 您可以在手機 App 上兌換這張電子折價券。

examples.en: Clip the paper coupons from the weekly grocery circular to save money.
examples.zh: 剪下每週超市促銷傳單上的紙本折價券以節省開銷。

examples.en: The restaurant gave each diner a buy-one-get-one-free dessert coupon.
examples.zh: 餐廳贈送每位用餐客人一張甜點買一送一優惠券。

explains.en: This noun means a paper or digital ticket that gives a lower price or special offer. A store may set a date or limit for its use. It can help a customer save money.
A shopper shows a code on a phone at checkout. The price of soap goes down. The offer only works this week.
A magazine includes a small paper slip for a discount. The customer cuts it out and takes it to a shop. The noun names this offer.

examples.en: Generations of families gather under the open courtyard of the brick Sanheyuan during festivals.
examples.zh: 逢年過節全家族老少齊聚在閩南紅磚三合院開闊的門前埕斗（Courtyard）擺設流水席，共享天倫之樂。

examples.en: Cool mountain breezes circulate naturally through the central courtyard, keeping the rooms fresh in summer.
examples.zh: 夏日傍晚清涼的山風在傳統院落的三合院中庭天井間自然對流穿梭，讓各個廂房即便不開冷氣也十分涼爽。

examples.en: We set up banquet tables across the brick courtyard to celebrate Grandma's ninetieth birthday.
examples.zh: 我們在紅磚合院開闊的門埕上擺開數十張總鋪師大紅辦桌，全庄熱鬧歡慶阿嬤的九十大壽。

entries.definition: 傳統三合院埕斗天井；中庭

explains.en: This noun means an open area surrounded by buildings or walls. It may be found inside a home, school, or public building. People use it to rest or walk outside.
A house has a small open space in the middle. Rooms face toward it. Sunlight reaches the plants there.
Students sit outside between classes. The area is surrounded by school buildings. The noun names this outdoor space.

examples.en: It was cowardly to blame someone who could not answer.
examples.zh: 把責任推給無法回應的人是懦弱的行為。

examples.en: The cowardly thief ran when the lights came on.
examples.zh: 燈亮起時，懦弱的小偷逃跑了。

examples.en: She called the attack cowardly and unfair.
examples.zh: 她稱這次攻擊既懦弱又不公平。

entries.definition: （形）懦弱的；膽小的；缺乏勇氣的

explains.en: This adjective describes someone who lacks courage when facing danger or difficulty. It can also describe an action that is unfair because a person avoids a direct fight. The word criticizes behavior.
A person leaves a friend behind when danger appears. The friend expected help. Others may call this action weak and unfair.
A bully hurts someone when no one is watching and then hides. The behavior avoids taking responsibility. The adjective describes this kind of action.

examples.en: The small bedroom feels warm, quiet, and cozy during winter.
examples.zh: 這間小臥室在冬天讓人感到溫暖、寧靜且溫馨愜意。

examples.en: We sat in a cozy corner of the vintage cafe reading novels and sipping tea.
examples.zh: 我們坐在這家復古咖啡館溫馨的一角看小說、喝熱茶。

examples.en: Put on a pair of cozy fleece slippers after kicking off your work boots.
examples.zh: 脫下工作皮靴後，換上一雙暖和舒適的刷毛室內拖鞋。

explains.en: This adjective describes a place that feels warm, comfortable, and pleasant. It can also describe a close and friendly feeling. The word is common for rooms and small homes.
A small room has soft chairs, warm light, and a blanket. A person enjoys reading there on a rainy day. The room feels comfortable.
Friends sit close together around a table and talk quietly. The setting feels welcoming. The adjective describes this warm atmosphere.

examples.en: The city announced a crackdown on illegal parking.
examples.zh: 市政府宣布嚴格取締違法停車。

examples.en: The crackdown led to several arrests.
examples.zh: 這波強力打擊行動造成數人被捕。

examples.en: Officials began a crackdown on fake medicine.
examples.zh: 官員開始嚴厲打擊假藥。

explains.en: This noun means a strong effort by authorities to stop illegal or unwanted behavior. It often includes stricter rules, checks, or punishments. The action may target crime or rule breaking.
Police inspect cars after many unsafe races occur. Drivers who break the law receive tickets. The enforcement becomes much stricter.
A school begins checking bags after students bring banned items. The new checks aim to stop the behavior. The noun names this strong action.

examples.en: She ate a cracker with a slice of cheese.
examples.zh: 她吃了一片餅乾，配上一片起司。

examples.en: The children pulled a party cracker together.
examples.zh: 孩子們一起拉開了派對拉炮。

examples.en: He used a nut cracker to open the shell.
examples.zh: 他用堅果夾打開外殼。

entries.definition: （名）薄脆餅乾；爆竹；破解密碼或系統的人或工具，依語境判斷。

explains.en: This noun can mean a thin, dry, crisp food often eaten with cheese or soup. It can also mean a device that makes a loud noise or something that breaks a hard shell. Context shows the meaning.
A child eats a small flat snack with cheese. It breaks with a dry sound. The food is simple and not sweet.
A holiday party uses a paper tube that pops when pulled. A nut tool can also open a hard shell. The noun has several uses.

examples.en: He tried to cram all the clothes into one suitcase.
examples.zh: 他試著把所有衣服塞進一個行李箱。

examples.en: I had to cram for the test last night.
examples.zh: 我昨晚只好臨時抱佛腳準備考試。

examples.en: The small bus was crammed with passengers.
examples.zh: 小巴士裡擠滿了乘客。

entries.definition: 塞滿；硬塞；臨時抱佛腳；死記。

explains.en: This verb means to push many things into a small space. It can also mean to study a lot in a short time, often before a test. The action is rushed or crowded.
A student puts too many books into one bag. The zipper barely closes. The items have been forced into the small space.
A learner reads notes late the night before an exam. There is little time to review. The verb describes this hurried study.

examples.en: A cramp in my leg woke me up.
examples.zh: 我腿部的抽筋把我痛醒了。

examples.en: The tight shoes cramped her toes.
examples.zh: 太緊的鞋子擠壓了她的腳趾。

examples.en: He stopped running because of a cramp.
examples.zh: 他因為抽筋而停止跑步。

entries.definition: （名）抽筋；痙攣；（動）使抽筋；限制活動

explains.en: This noun means a sudden painful tightening in a muscle. It can make movement difficult for a short time. As a verb, it can mean to limit space or freedom.
A runner stops and holds one leg after a race. The muscle feels tight and painful. It may take a few minutes to relax.
A crowded desk leaves little room for a person to write. The lack of space makes work harder. The verb can describe this limitation.

examples.en: The hikers stood near the edge of the crater.
examples.zh: 健行者站在火山口邊緣附近。

examples.en: A meteor made a crater on the moon.
examples.zh: 隕石在月球上撞出了一個坑洞。

examples.en: The old volcano has a broad crater.
examples.zh: 這座古老火山有一個寬闊的火山口。

entries.definition: （名）火山口；隕石坑；（動）形成坑洞

explains.en: This noun means a large bowl-shaped hole in the ground. It may be made by a volcano or by an object from space hitting the earth. The surface around it can be rough.
A volcano erupts and leaves a deep round hole at its top. Steam rises from the opening. Visitors can see the rim from far away.
A space rock strikes the moon and leaves a wide hollow mark. There is no water inside it. The noun names this kind of hole.

examples.en: The witness gave a credible account of the event.
examples.zh: 證人對事件提出了可信的說明。

examples.en: Her explanation sounded credible to the group.
examples.zh: 她的解釋聽起來讓大家信服。

examples.en: The report offered credible evidence.
examples.zh: 這份報告提供了可信的證據。

entries.definition: （形）可信的、可靠的；有足夠證據或品質使人相信。

explains.en: This adjective describes something that seems likely to be true or believable. A person may be trusted because of knowledge or honesty. Evidence can make an account seem stronger.
A witness gives a clear account and has no reason to lie. The details match what others saw. People believe the story.
A news report names its sources and shows proof. Readers can check the facts. The adjective describes information that seems trustworthy.

examples.en: A crocodile rested on the riverbank.
examples.zh: 一隻鱷魚在河岸上休息。

examples.en: The guide warned us to stay away from the crocodile.
examples.zh: 導遊提醒我們遠離那隻鱷魚。

examples.en: A crocodile can swim with its tail.
examples.zh: 鱷魚能用尾巴游泳。

entries.definition: 鱷魚；大型半水生爬行動物。

explains.en: This noun names a large reptile with a long body, strong tail, and powerful jaws. It lives in rivers and wetlands in warm parts of the world. It often waits quietly near water.
A large animal lies still beside a river. Only its eyes and nose show above the water. It can move quickly to catch prey.
A young one leaves the nest and follows its mother toward a pond. Its skin is covered with hard scales. The reptile grows very large.

examples.en: Use the crossing to reach the other side of the street.
examples.zh: 請走行人穿越道到街道另一側。

examples.en: The ferry crossing took twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 渡輪航程花了二十分鐘。

examples.en: A crossing guard helped the children cross safely.
examples.zh: 導護人員協助孩子們安全過馬路。

entries.definition: （名）十字路口；穿越處；交叉點；渡口

explains.en: This noun means a place where people or vehicles can go from one side to another. It often refers to a marked area on a road or a route over water. It can also name the act of moving across.
A person waits for the light before walking across a busy street. White lines show where to go. Cars stop to let people pass.
A boat carries people from one side of a river to the other. The trip takes a few minutes. The noun can name this journey.

examples.en: He used crutches while his ankle healed.
examples.zh: 腳踝復原期間，他使用拐杖行走。

examples.en: She placed one crutch beside the chair.
examples.zh: 她把一支拐杖放在椅子旁。

examples.en: The speaker used his notes as a crutch.
examples.zh: 那位講者過度依賴筆記。

entries.definition: （名）拐杖；精神支柱；（動）依賴……支撐

explains.en: This is a support that helps someone walk when a leg is hurt. The person holds it while taking steps. It carries some of their weight.
A person with a broken leg may use two long supports to move around. Each has a handle for the hand. The supports help the person keep weight off the injured leg.
The word can also mean something a person relies on too much. A student may always read from notes instead of learning to speak freely. The notes become a way to avoid doing the harder task.

examples.en: The bear cub slept beside its mother.
examples.zh: 小熊睡在媽媽身旁。

examples.en: Two lion cubs played in the grass.
examples.zh: 兩隻小獅子在草地上玩耍。

examples.en: A fox cub peered out of the den.
examples.zh: 一隻小狐狸從洞穴裡向外張望。

entries.definition: （名）幼獸；尤其指熊、獅子等大型哺乳動物的幼崽。

explains.en: This is a young animal such as a bear, lion, or fox. It is smaller than its parents. Its mother may feed and protect it.
A baby bear may stay close to its mother in the forest. It plays and learns how to find food. This word names the young animal.
A young lion may play with others of its own age. Its soft fur may have spots. It grows into a large cat as it gets older.

examples.en: She sliced a cucumber for the salad.
examples.zh: 她切了一條小黃瓜做沙拉。

examples.en: We grow cucumbers beside the fence.
examples.zh: 我們在圍籬旁種小黃瓜。

examples.en: The sandwich had thin cucumber slices inside.
examples.zh: 三明治裡夾著薄薄的小黃瓜片。

explains.en: This is a long vegetable with green skin and a pale inside. It contains a lot of water. People often slice it into salads.
You can cut this green food into thin rounds. The inside has small seeds. It tastes mild and feels crisp when fresh.
This plant grows along the ground or climbs a support. Its long fruits can be eaten fresh. Some are kept in salty or sour liquid to make pickles.

examples.en: Organic tea growers cultivate heirloom bushes using natural compost and mountain spring irrigation.
examples.zh: 堅持友善大地的有機茶農以天然堆肥與甘冽山泉水悉心灌溉茶樹，在天地滋養下涵育頂級茶菁。

examples.en: Reading classic literature from around the world helps cultivate critical thinking and emotional depth.
examples.zh: 廣泛閱讀世界古典文學與哲學經典名作，有助於涵養青年的獨立批判性思維與深厚的人文同理心。

examples.en: Forward-thinking companies actively cultivate collaborative working cultures where constructive dissent is welcomed.
examples.zh: 具備前瞻遠見的跨國企業主動培育包容開放的協作文化，由衷鼓勵員工提出多元具建設性的不同聲音。

entries.definition: 細心栽種茶樹；涵養品味

explains.en: This means to prepare land and grow plants on it. A farmer may loosen the soil and plant seeds. The work helps crops grow.
Someone can care for plants over a long period. They may give the plants water and remove unwanted growth. The verb describes this careful growing process.
The word can also mean to develop a skill, quality, or relationship. A child may slowly build a love of reading. Regular attention helps that interest grow.

examples.en: The chart shows our cumulative sales for the year.
examples.zh: 圖表顯示我們今年的累計銷售額。

examples.en: The teacher added up the cumulative scores.
examples.zh: 老師把累計分數加總起來。

examples.en: Small changes can have a cumulative effect.
examples.zh: 小改變可能產生累積的影響。

entries.definition: （形）累積的；逐漸增加的；總合的

explains.en: This describes something that grows as more parts are added over time. Small amounts join together to make a larger total. The final amount includes the earlier parts.
A student earns points each week. At the end of the term, all the points count toward one total. The adjective describes that growing total.
One small change may have little effect. Many such changes over several years can have a large effect. This word describes their combined result.

examples.en: Please park close to the curb.
examples.zh: 請靠近路緣停車。

examples.en: The city wants to curb traffic near the school.
examples.zh: 市府想減少學校附近的車流。

examples.en: He tried to curb his spending on snacks.
examples.zh: 他試著控制買零食的花費。

entries.definition: （名）路緣；控制措施；（動）抑制；控制

explains.en: This is the raised edge between a road and the path beside it. It helps mark where vehicles should travel. A person steps over it when leaving the sidewalk.
As a verb, this means to limit or control something. A town may try to reduce traffic in its center. Rules can help keep the amount down.
A person may try to hold back a strong feeling or habit. Someone who talks a lot may practice listening more. The action keeps that behavior under control.

examples.en: The city announced a curfew after the storm.
examples.zh: 暴風雨過後，市府宣布實施宵禁。

examples.en: My parents set my curfew at ten o’clock.
examples.zh: 爸媽規定我十點前必須回家。

examples.en: Everyone returned to the hotel before curfew.
examples.zh: 大家都在規定時間前回到飯店。

entries.definition: （名）宵禁；規定人們必須待在室內或停止外出的時間。

explains.en: This is a rule that people must stay inside after a certain time. A city may use it during an emergency. The rule states when people can go out again.
A family may set a time when a child must be home. The child needs to return before that time. This word can name that household rule.
A school trip may require everyone to be back in their rooms by ten. Students cannot go out after that hour. The rule limits evening movement.

examples.en: We ate vegetable curry with rice.
examples.zh: 我們吃了蔬菜咖哩配飯。

examples.en: This chicken curry is mild enough for me.
examples.zh: 這道雞肉咖哩的辣度對我來說很溫和。

examples.en: She added potatoes to the curry.
examples.zh: 她在咖哩裡加了馬鈴薯。

entries.definition: 咖哩；咖哩料理；用咖哩調味。

explains.en: This is a dish cooked with a mixture of spices. It may contain vegetables, meat, or beans. People often eat it with rice or bread.
