examples.en: The company used a hedge against rising costs.
examples.zh: 公司採取避險措施以防成本上升。

examples.en: They planted a hedge along the front path.
examples.zh: 他們沿著前方小徑種了一排樹籬。

entries.definition: （名）樹籬；（動）用樹籬圍住；也指避免承諾或降低風險。

explains.en: As a noun, this is a row of bushes planted to mark a boundary or hide a view. A garden may have one beside a path. The plants form a natural screen.
As a verb, it means to reduce the effect of a loss or risk. A shop may keep extra supplies in case of delay. The backup offers protection.
As a noun, this can mean something that reduces the risk of loss. A farmer may grow several crops instead of relying on one. If one fails, the others can still provide food or money.

examples.en: The music heightened the suspense in the film.
examples.zh: 音樂提高了電影中的緊張感。

examples.en: The bright scarf heightened the contrast with her coat.
examples.zh: 亮色圍巾讓它和外套的對比更加明顯。

examples.en: A sudden silence heightened everyone's curiosity.
examples.zh: 突然的沉默加深了大家的好奇心。

entries.definition: 提高；加強；使更明顯；變得更強烈。

explains.en: This verb means to make something stronger or more intense. A rising drumbeat can build excitement. The feeling becomes more noticeable.
A speaker may use a louder voice to make a point stand out. The attention grows stronger. The word describes an increase in force or effect.
A contrast between light and dark can become more striking. The difference is made sharper. This verb applies to feelings, sounds, colors, and events.

examples.en: Winter begins in the Southern Hemisphere in June.
examples.zh: 南半球的冬天在六月開始。

examples.en: The equator divides Earth into two hemispheres.
examples.zh: 赤道把地球分成兩個半球。

examples.en: Most of the country lies in the northern hemisphere.
examples.zh: 該國大部分位於北半球。

entries.definition: （名）半球；地球或大腦的一半區域

explains.en: This noun means one half of the Earth, usually divided by the equator or a line of longitude. Maps show the northern and southern parts. Each half is a large region.
The Earth has two halves separated by the equator. Seasons occur at opposite times in the two regions. The term helps describe global locations.
The word can also refer to half of a sphere or another rounded object. A globe can be split into two equal parts. The context identifies which world is meant.

examples.en: The heroic rescue saved two hikers.
examples.zh: 英勇的救援行動救了兩名登山客。

examples.en: She made a heroic effort to finish the race.
examples.zh: 她英勇地努力完成比賽。

examples.en: The firefighter's heroic actions inspired the town.
examples.zh: 消防員英勇的行動鼓舞了整座城鎮。

entries.definition: （形）英勇的；有英雄氣概的；值得敬佩的。

explains.en: This adjective describes a person or action that shows great courage or noble effort. A firefighter may enter a dangerous place to help others. The action is admired.
A character may risk personal safety to protect a friend. The brave choice becomes an important part of a story. The word praises courage and selflessness.
It can also describe an attempt that is ambitious and difficult. A team may try to save an old building. The effort is worthy of respect even if it fails.

examples.en: The documentary explains the dangers of heroin.
examples.zh: 這部紀錄片說明了海洛因的危險。

examples.en: Police seized heroin during the investigation.
examples.zh: 警方在調查期間查獲海洛因。

examples.en: The clinic offers support to people recovering from heroin addiction.
examples.zh: 診所為正在戒除海洛因成癮的人提供協助。

entries.definition: （名）海洛因；一種高度成癮且危害健康的非法鴉片類藥物。

explains.en: This noun names a powerful illegal drug made from a substance found in the opium poppy. It can cause severe dependence. Laws in many places forbid it.
Doctors once used the substance in medicine, but it carries serious risks. It can slow breathing and cause overdose. Public health discussions often mention its dangers.
The drug may be injected, smoked, or taken in other ways. Its use can harm the body and affect daily life. The word refers to this specific substance.

examples.en: The novel follows a heterosexual couple in a small town.
examples.zh: 這本小說描寫一對住在小鎮的異性戀伴侶。

examples.en: He identifies as heterosexual.
examples.zh: 他認同自己是異性戀。

examples.en: The survey asked about heterosexual relationships.
examples.zh: 這份調查詢問了異性戀關係。

explains.en: This adjective describes a person who is romantically or sexually attracted to people of a different gender. The term can describe an identity. Individuals may choose their own labels.
A person with this orientation may form a relationship with someone of another gender. The word is a formal descriptive term. It does not tell someone's personality.
The word can also describe a relationship or couple involving partners of different genders. Context determines whether it describes a person or a relationship. It names the nature of their bond.

examples.en: The office hierarchy has four management levels.
examples.zh: 辦公室的組織層級有四層管理職位。

examples.en: She moved up the hierarchy after years of work.
examples.zh: 多年工作後，她在組織階層中晉升。

examples.en: The chart shows the hierarchy of the animal groups.
examples.zh: 這張圖表顯示動物類群的分類層次。

entries.definition: （名）階層；等級制度；依上下位排列的系統

explains.en: This noun means a system in which people or things are ranked from higher to lower levels. A school may have classes with different authority roles. Each position has a place.
A company can have workers, managers, and directors with different responsibilities. The structure shows who makes decisions. This arrangement is an organized ranking system.
The word can describe categories in nature or ideas too. A library may arrange books from broad groups to smaller ones. The levels form an ordered structure.

examples.en: Criminals tried to hijack the bus.
examples.zh: 歹徒企圖劫持那輛公車。

examples.en: A hacker hijacked the television signal.
examples.zh: 駭客劫持了電視訊號。

examples.en: The police stopped a plan to hijack the plane.
examples.zh: 警方阻止了一起劫機計畫。

entries.definition: （動）劫持；挾持；強行控制；（名）劫持事件

explains.en: This verb means to take control of a vehicle or aircraft by force. A person may threaten those aboard. The act is a serious crime.
The word can also mean to take over a broadcast or online system. Someone may interrupt normal programming. The action changes who controls the service.
A story may describe criminals taking a plane and demanding something. The verb focuses on gaining control by force. It can apply to other vehicles too.

examples.en: He sounded hoarse after the concert.
examples.zh: 演唱會後他的聲音變得沙啞。

examples.en: The child had a hoarse voice from crying.
examples.zh: 孩子哭得聲音沙啞。

examples.en: She whispered in a hoarse voice.
examples.zh: 她用沙啞的聲音低語。

entries.definition: （形）沙啞的；聲音粗糙、失去平常清晰度的。

explains.en: This adjective describes a voice that sounds rough or unclear, often because of a sore throat. A person may struggle to speak. The sound is lower and scratchy.
After cheering loudly at a game, someone's voice may become rough. The change can be temporary. The adjective describes how the voice sounds.
The word may describe sound from a speaker or machine too. Static can make words difficult to understand. It suggests a rough quality rather than a smooth tone.

examples.en: The film tells the story of a homosexual man in the 1950s.
examples.zh: 這部電影講述一名生活在 1950 年代的男同志的故事。

examples.en: She is a homosexual woman who writes about her community.
examples.zh: 她是一位書寫自身社群的女同志。

examples.en: The book examines homosexual relationships in history.
examples.zh: 這本書探討歷史上的同性戀關係。

explains.en: This adjective describes a person who is romantically or sexually attracted to people of the same gender. The term can describe an identity. Individuals may choose how they identify.
A person with this orientation may build a relationship with a same-gender partner. The word is often used in formal writing. It says nothing about character or interests.

The adjective can also describe a relationship or community involving people with this orientation. Context reveals whether it refers to a person, group, or partnership. It names the nature of their bond.

examples.en: She received an honorary degree from the university.
examples.zh: 她獲得大學頒發的榮譽學位。

examples.en: The mayor named him honorary chair of the festival.
examples.zh: 市長任命他為藝術節的名譽主席。

examples.en: An honorary member attended the club's annual dinner.
examples.zh: 一位名譽會員出席了俱樂部的年度晚宴。

entries.definition: （形）榮譽的；名譽上的；無薪酬而授予的

explains.en: This adjective means given as an honor, without the usual duties or pay. A university may give a respected guest a special title. The person is recognized rather than hired for daily work.
A person can have a role that is mostly symbolic. They may attend an event but not manage the organization. The label shows respect.

It can describe a degree or title given to recognize someone’s work. The person receives the honor without completing the usual course or taking on a regular job. This kind of recognition may reward past service or skill.

examples.en: Our hospitable neighbors invited us for tea.
examples.zh: 熱情好客的鄰居邀請我們喝茶。

examples.en: The island is known for its hospitable people.
examples.zh: 這座島以熱情好客的居民聞名。

examples.en: The host was hospitable to every visitor.
examples.zh: 主人熱情款待每一位訪客。

entries.definition: （形）好客的；宜居的；適合生長的

explains.en: This adjective describes a person who welcomes guests warmly. A host may offer visitors food and a comfortable seat. The guest feels at ease.
A country or town can be described this way when visitors are treated kindly. People may give directions or share local customs. Their friendliness makes newcomers feel welcome.
The word can describe an open and generous attitude. Someone may invite a new neighbor for tea. It focuses on kindness to guests.

examples.en: Taiwanese warmth and generous hospitality leave deep impressions on tourists.
examples.zh: 台灣人發自內心的濃濃人情味與熱情好客，給全球各國觀光客留下了深刻感動。

examples.en: She pursued a degree in hospitality management to learn international hotel operations.
examples.zh: 她在大學攻讀觀光餐旅管理學位，以深入研習五星級國際連鎖飯店的運營精髓。

examples.en: Thank you for welcoming our team with such heartwarming generosity and hospitality.
examples.zh: 由衷感謝您以如此溫暖體貼的深厚善意與熱情款待，熱烈迎接我們團隊的到訪。

examples.en: In Taiwan, offering a freshly brewed cup of hot oolong is the ultimate gesture of warm hospitality.
examples.zh: 在台灣，每逢客人進門便親切奉上一杯剛沖泡好的熱騰騰高山烏龍茶，是台灣人最溫暖厚道的人情味。

examples.en: The mountain bed-and-breakfast owners touched our hearts with their generous hospitality and local breakfast.
examples.zh: 隱身於清境農場的山莊民宿主人親切純樸的待客熱忱與手作豐盛在地早餐，深深溫暖了每位旅人的心房。

examples.en: She built a rewarding corporate career across the international luxury hotel and hospitality sector.
examples.zh: 憑藉著出色的跨文化溝通能力，她在國際頂級五星級連鎖飯店與款待管理產業中開拓了輝煌的職涯格局。

examples.en: True coffee culture marries technical brewing perfection with warm, welcoming customer hospitality.
examples.zh: 真正的精品咖啡文化，將極致嚴謹的沖煮科學與熱情溫暖的職人款待之道完美融合。

examples.en: The neighborhood cafe is celebrated for its genuine hospitality, remembering regulars by their names.
examples.zh: 這家隱身巷弄的老街角咖啡館以其真誠質樸的款待熱情聞名，親切叫出每位常客的名字與喜好。

examples.en: Thoughtful hospitality turns a simple morning beverage into an uplifting personal connection.
examples.zh: 充滿溫度、體貼入微的職人真摯款待，能將一杯看似平凡的晨間咖啡昇華為撫慰人心的心靈連結。

examples.en: Flawless dining requires intuitive front-of-house hospitality that anticipates every guest's unspoken desire.
examples.zh: 完美的頂級用餐體驗，仰賴外場團隊「春風化雨的真摯款待」（Hospitality），在客人開口前即洞察每項需求。

examples.en: Taiwanese residents are renowned internationally for their warm, sincere, and helpful hospitality to foreign visitors.
examples.zh: 台灣民眾待人接物溫暖熱情、樂善好施的誠摯好客之道，在國際旅人間樹立了有口皆碑的優良美譽。

examples.en: Graduates with degrees in international hospitality management are recruited by luxury resort chains globally.
examples.zh: 擁有國際餐旅觀光管理碩士學位的高材生，長年受到全球各大頂級五星級連鎖奢華度假村競相爭聘。

entries.definition: 款待熱情；好客；餐旅觀光業；奉茶熱情待客之道；殷勤好客；溫暖傳遞每杯咖啡產區故事之真摯款待；米其林三星春風化雨、無微不至之款待哲學

explains.en: This noun means friendly treatment offered to guests or visitors. A family may welcome a traveler into their home. They offer comfort and care.
Hotels and restaurants work in an industry that serves travelers. Staff greet guests and provide rooms or meals. The word names this kind of service.
The term can also describe kindness shown to strangers. A warm welcome makes a guest feel included. It is a quality as well as a type of work.

examples.en: Doctors decided to hospitalize the injured cyclist.
examples.zh: 醫師決定讓受傷的自行車騎士住院。

examples.en: The child was hospitalized for two days.
examples.zh: 那名孩子住院兩天。

examples.en: Doctors may hospitalize patients who need close care.
examples.zh: 醫師可能會讓需要密切照護的病人住院。

entries.definition: （動）使住院；安排病人入院接受治療或照護。

explains.en: This verb means to admit someone to a hospital for medical care. A doctor may arrange a bed for a patient. The stay can be short or long.
A person may need hospital care after an accident. Staff record the admission and provide treatment. The verb describes entering a medical facility as a patient.
The word can also describe sending someone into a hospital. News reports may use it when discussing a public figure's condition. It is a formal medical term.

examples.en: We stayed at a hostel near the train station.
examples.zh: 我們住在火車站附近的一間青年旅館。

examples.en: The hostel has a shared kitchen for guests.
examples.zh: 這間青年旅館有供房客使用的共用廚房。

examples.en: Two travelers met in the hostel common room.
examples.zh: 兩名旅客在青年旅館的交誼廳相遇。

entries.definition: 青年旅舍；宿舍；簡易旅館。

explains.en: This noun means a low-cost place where travelers can sleep. Guests often share rooms or common areas. It may have bunk beds and a kitchen.
Students on a trip may choose this kind of lodging to save money. People from different places can meet there. The atmosphere may be casual.
The term can also refer to a simple lodging house in some countries. It offers basic rooms rather than luxury service. Travelers use it for a short stay.

examples.en: The helicopter hovered above the field.
examples.zh: 直升機在田野上空盤旋。

examples.en: A hummingbird hovered near the flower.
examples.zh: 蜂鳥在花朵旁停留飛舞。

examples.en: She hovered by the door while we packed.
examples.zh: 我們收拾行李時，她一直在門邊等候。

entries.definition: （動）盤旋；徘徊；猶豫不決；（名）短暫停留

explains.en: This verb means to remain in the air or stay near one place without moving far. A helicopter can do this above a field. A bird may hold its position on moving air.
A small insect may stay close to a flower. It keeps moving its wings while remaining in roughly the same spot. The verb describes that position.
The word can also mean to wait near someone or something. A parent may stay close while a child plays. It suggests lingering nearby.

examples.en: The coach did not humiliate the player after the mistake.
examples.zh: 球員犯錯後，教練沒有羞辱他。

examples.en: A mean comment humiliated her in front of the class.
examples.zh: 一句刻薄的評論讓她在全班面前感到羞辱。

examples.en: He apologized for humiliating his friend.
examples.zh: 他為羞辱朋友而道歉。

explains.en: This verb means to make someone feel deeply ashamed or foolish. A cruel joke may embarrass a classmate in front of others. The effect can hurt.
A person may be made to feel small after a public mistake. Others should treat such situations with care. The verb describes causing strong shame.
The word is stronger than simply making someone feel awkward. It suggests that their dignity has been damaged. The action can happen through words or behavior.

examples.en: She had a hunch that the keys were in the car.
examples.zh: 她直覺鑰匙可能在車裡。

examples.en: The old man walked with a slight hunch.
examples.zh: 老人走路時背部微微駝起。

examples.en: I hunch over my desk when I draw.
examples.zh: 我畫圖時會彎身趴在書桌前。

entries.definition: （名）直覺、預感；駝背姿勢；（動）彎腰或縮起身體。

explains.en: As a noun, this is a rounded upper back caused by bending forward. A person may sit with this posture. It changes the shape of the shoulders.
It can also mean a guess or idea based on incomplete clues. Someone may suspect where a missing toy is. This is not certain knowledge.
As a verb, it means to bend the back or make a guess. A student may bend forward to hear better. The context indicates posture or suspicion.

examples.en: The fallen branch was a hurdle on the path.
examples.zh: 掉落的樹枝成了路上的障礙。

examples.en: Cost was the biggest hurdle for the project.
examples.zh: 成本是這個專案最大的障礙。

examples.en: She cleared the final hurdle and won the race.
examples.zh: 她跨過最後一道欄架，贏得了比賽。

explains.en: This noun means something that blocks progress or makes a task harder. A fallen tree can block a road. The obstacle must be dealt with before people continue.
In a race, a barrier is something runners jump over. The event tests speed and skill. The same noun can describe a problem in plans.
A person may face difficulties while learning a new skill. Each problem can feel like a barrier. The word names the challenge that must be crossed.

examples.en: Plug-in hybrid cars combine gasoline engines with rechargeable electric motors.
examples.zh: 插電式油電混合動力車巧妙結合了傳統燃油引擎與可外接充電的電動馬達。

examples.en: Many taxi drivers prefer driving a hybrid because of its outstanding city fuel economy.
examples.zh: 許多計程車運將偏好開油電混合車，因為它在市區行駛時具有極佳的省油表現。

examples.en: The university offers a hybrid learning model blending in-person lectures with online webinars.
examples.zh: 這所大學提供了結合實體面授課堂與線上視訊講座的混合式學習模式。

entries.definition: 油電混合動力車；混合的

explains.en: This noun or adjective describes something made from two different kinds of things. A plant may have parents from two related varieties. Its features come from both.
A car can use both electricity and fuel to move. The combined design uses two energy sources. The word describes this mixed system.
In biology, a living thing with parents from different breeds may have a blend of traits. The term also applies to mixed methods or designs. Both parts contribute to its design.

examples.en: Rigorous hand hygiene protocols and UV sterilization robots eliminate hospital-acquired infections.
examples.zh: 落實嚴格的「內外夾弓大立腕」洗手衛生規範（Hygiene）搭配紫外線消毒機器人，徹底阻斷院內交叉感染。

examples.en: Proper dental hygiene requires brushing twice daily, cleaning with floss, and scheduling routine cleanings.
examples.zh: 良好的口腔牙齒個人衛生習慣，在於每天早晚確實刷牙、搭配牙線清除齒縫殘渣，並每半年定期洗牙檢查。

examples.en: Food safety inspectors shut down the restaurant kitchen due to shocking failures in basic food preparation hygiene.
examples.zh: 衛生局食品藥物管理稽查大隊在突擊檢查中，發現該熱門餐廳後廚存在嚴重的食材保鮮與環境衛生違規，當場勒令停業。

entries.definition: 院內感染管制洗手衛生規範

explains.en: This noun means practices that keep the body, food, or surroundings clean and healthy. Washing hands is one example. Clean habits can help prevent illness.
Schools teach children how to brush teeth and handle food safely. These routines support health. The word can refer to personal or public cleanliness.
A kitchen needs clean surfaces and safe food storage. Good practices reduce the spread of germs. The noun describes the habits and conditions involved.

examples.en: The hypocrite preached honesty but often lied.
examples.zh: 那個偽君子宣揚誠實，自己卻常常說謊。

examples.en: No one trusted the hypocrite after the truth came out.
examples.zh: 真相揭露後，沒有人再相信那個偽善者。

examples.en: The story's hypocrite judged others unfairly.
examples.zh: 故事中的偽君子不公平地批評別人。

explains.en: This noun means a person who claims to have good beliefs but acts against them. Someone may speak kindly while treating others unfairly. The behavior reveals a mismatch.
A character may criticize others for lying while hiding the truth. Readers may notice the double standard. The noun describes that person.
The word often expresses strong disapproval. It points to a difference between what a person says and does. Honest behavior matches stated values.

examples.en: The ship passed safely beside the iceberg.
examples.zh: 船隻安全地從冰山旁駛過。

examples.en: Only the tip of the iceberg showed above the water.
examples.zh: 只有冰山的一角露出水面。

examples.en: The report revealed an iceberg of hidden costs.
examples.zh: 報告揭露了龐大隱藏成本中的一小部分。

explains.en: This noun names a huge piece of ice floating in the sea. Most of its mass is underwater. Only a small part can be seen above the surface.
It breaks off from a glacier or ice shelf and drifts through cold water. Ships watch for these floating blocks. Their hidden size makes them dangerous.
The word is also used figuratively for a problem with much more beneath the surface. A visible issue may be only a small part. The comparison comes from the ice's hidden mass.

examples.en: Lanterns illuminated the garden path.
examples.zh: 燈籠照亮了花園小徑。

examples.en: The chart illuminated the main idea.
examples.zh: 圖表讓主要概念更清楚。

examples.en: Sunlight illuminated the old stone wall.
examples.zh: 陽光照亮了古老的石牆。

entries.definition: （動）照亮、闡明；提供光線或使意思更清楚。

explains.en: This verb means to provide light or make something brighter. A lamp can brighten a dark room. The details become easier to see.
It can also mean to explain an idea clearly. A teacher may use a diagram to help students understand. The explanation makes the topic clearer.
A building can be lit up for a celebration. Bright colors may draw attention to it. The verb describes adding light or clarity.

examples.en: The dark sky warned of imminent rain.
examples.zh: 陰暗的天空預示著大雨即將來臨。

examples.en: An announcement about the imminent closure surprised the staff.
examples.zh: 即將關閉的消息讓員工感到驚訝。

examples.en: The team prepared for an imminent change in schedule.
examples.zh: 團隊為即將到來的行程變更做好準備。

explains.en: This adjective describes something that is likely to happen very soon. Dark clouds may signal a storm. People expect it in the near future.
A deadline can be close at hand. A teacher may remind students that a report is due soon. The word stresses that little time remains.
The term can describe danger or change approaching. It has not happened yet, but the signs suggest it is close. Context shows what is expected.

examples.en: Kant’s categorical imperative commands humans to never treat fellow persons merely as a means.
examples.zh: 康德哲學中的「絕對命令」（Categorical Imperative）告誡世人：永遠要將他人視為目的本身，而非獲利工具。

examples.en: Immediate global climate action is an urgent humanitarian imperative to save low-lying island nations.
examples.zh: 立即採取全球跨國氣候行動，是一項刻不容緩的人道主義迫切使命，以拯救面臨滅頂之災的海島國家。

examples.en: In grammar, imperative sentences are used to issue direct commands, friendly requests, or firm warnings.
examples.zh: 在英語文法結構中，「祈使句」（Imperative Sentence）通常用於發出直接的行動命令、委婉請求或嚴肅警示。

entries.definition: 康德絕對命令道德義務；迫切的

explains.en: This adjective means absolutely necessary or very important. A ticket may be required to enter a concert. Without it, entry is not possible.
The word can also describe a command or strong need. A rule may require everyone to wear a badge. The instruction must be followed.
As a noun, it can refer to an urgent need or command. A teacher may say it is essential to finish a task. The exact use depends on the sentence.

examples.en: The museum displayed imperial coins from ancient Rome.
examples.zh: 博物館展出了古羅馬帝國的錢幣。

examples.en: The palace had an imperial entrance hall.
examples.zh: 宮殿有一座氣派的帝國式入口大廳。

examples.en: They studied the imperial system of measurement.
examples.zh: 他們研究了英制測量系統。

entries.definition: （形）帝國的；皇帝的；英制的；威嚴的

explains.en: This adjective relates to an empire or an emperor. A palace may have rooms in this style. The term connects with an empire or its history.
It can describe something very large or grand. A huge building may seem impressive. In this sense, it suggests a commanding scale.
Some systems use this adjective for units or measurements. The context may concern a historic government or a standard system. It relates to empire, grandeur, or measurement.

examples.en: Her implicit message was clear from her expression.
examples.zh: 從她的表情可以清楚看出她未明說的訊息。

examples.en: The rule contains an implicit promise of fairness.
examples.zh: 這條規則隱含著公平的承諾。

examples.en: There was an implicit warning in his quiet reply.
examples.zh: 他平靜的回答中帶著含蓄的警告。

explains.en: This adjective describes a meaning that is suggested but not stated directly. A person may imply that a plan is risky. Listeners understand the unstated idea.
A rule can contain an unstated assumption. Readers may need to think about what the writer expects them to know. The idea is present without direct wording.
A message may be understood from tone or context. The speaker does not say everything plainly. This adjective describes that indirect quality.

examples.en: The imposing tower could be seen from every corner of town.
examples.zh: 城鎮各處都能看見那座雄偉的塔樓。

examples.en: Her imposing voice quieted the noisy room.
examples.zh: 她威嚴的聲音讓吵鬧的房間安靜下來。

examples.en: An imposing gate marked the entrance to the palace.
examples.zh: 一座氣勢宏偉的大門標示出宮殿入口。

entries.definition: （形）雄偉壯觀的、令人敬畏的；體型或規模突出。

explains.en: This adjective describes something impressive because of its size, appearance, or manner. A tall building may dominate a street. People notice it immediately.
A person can have a serious, confident manner that makes others pay attention. Their presence seems strong. The word describes that effect.
A wall or mountain may look enormous from nearby. Its scale can inspire respect or awe. The adjective focuses on an impressive appearance.

examples.en: The judge could imprison the thief for a year.
examples.zh: 法官可能判處小偷一年監禁。

examples.en: The rebels imprisoned the captured soldier.
examples.zh: 叛軍囚禁了被俘的士兵。

examples.en: Independent constitutional courts ensure the state cannot arbitrarily imprison citizens without due process.
examples.zh: 獨立的憲法法院確保國家未經正當法律程序不得任意將公民監禁入獄。

explains.en: This verb means to put someone in a prison or another place where they cannot leave. A court may order a person to remain there. Freedom is taken away.
The noun names the act or period of keeping someone confined. A story may describe a long time behind locked doors. The word has a serious legal sense.
A person can also be held in a small space, such as a cell. The term describes confinement and loss of freedom. Context may refer to the act or state.

examples.en: The road inclines toward the river.
examples.zh: 道路朝河邊傾斜。

examples.en: She inclines toward drawing animals.
examples.zh: 她有畫動物的興趣傾向。

examples.en: The ramp has a slight incline.
examples.zh: 這條坡道有一點斜度。

entries.definition: （動）傾斜；使傾向於；（名）斜坡；傾向

explains.en: As a verb, this means to lean or slope in a particular direction. A road may rise toward a hill. The surface is not level.
As a noun, it can mean a sloping surface or hill. A road may climb a steep one toward the top. The word names the rising ground.
A chair may lean forward slightly. A path can also have a gentle slope. The word describes either the physical angle or a personal leaning.

examples.en: Building an inclusive workplace welcomes talents regardless of physical abilities.
examples.zh: 打造兼具多元、平等與共融（DEI）的友善職場環境，熱情接納不同背景的優秀人才。

examples.en: The resort offered an all-inclusive holiday package covering lodging, dining, and activities.
examples.zh: 這座海濱渡假村推出了一價全包式度假套裝行程，涵蓋了客房住宿、三餐精緻美饌與活動。

examples.en: An inclusive educational curriculum ensures that students of all backgrounds feel valued.
examples.zh: 兼具多元包容性的學校課程規劃，能確保讓來自各種多元文化背景的學生都感受到被尊重。

entries.definition: 多元共融的；包容的；包含全部的

explains.en: This adjective describes a group or activity that welcomes many kinds of people. A club may invite members of every age. Everyone has a place.
A book can use language that includes different experiences. Readers may see people like themselves in its pages. The word suggests openness and broad participation.
The term can describe a price or amount that already covers several parts. A fee may include meals and entry. In that sense, nothing extra is left out.

examples.en: The late return incurred an extra fee.
examples.zh: 逾期歸還產生了額外費用。

examples.en: The company incurred a loss during the winter.
examples.zh: 公司在冬季蒙受了損失。

examples.en: His careless action incurred a penalty.
examples.zh: 他粗心的行為招致了處罰。

explains.en: This verb means to experience or bring about an unwanted result, cost, or responsibility. A delay may create extra charges. The problem follows from an action.
A person may take on a debt by borrowing money. The obligation becomes theirs. The verb often appears in formal writing about costs or consequences.
A business decision can lead to a loss or penalty. The result is not necessarily planned. This verb describes becoming subject to an effect.

examples.en: Her indifference to the noise surprised her friends.
examples.zh: 她對噪音毫不在意，讓朋友感到驚訝。

examples.en: The audience showed indifference to the long speech.
examples.zh: 聽眾對冗長的演講顯得漠不關心。

examples.en: His indifference made the team feel ignored.
examples.zh: 他的冷漠讓團隊覺得被忽視。

entries.definition: （名）冷漠、不在乎；對某事缺少興趣或關心。

explains.en: This noun means a lack of interest, concern, or feeling about something. A person may ignore a community event. Their response seems unconcerned.
Someone may show little care about a problem affecting others. The attitude can disappoint friends. The word describes emotional distance or lack of attention.
The term differs from active dislike. A person with this attitude may simply feel nothing strongly. Their lack of response is the main feature.

examples.en: She was indignant about the unfair decision.
examples.zh: 她對不公平的決定感到憤慨。

examples.en: The coach grew indignant when the referee ignored the foul.
examples.zh: 裁判忽略犯規時，教練變得十分憤怒。

examples.en: His indignant reply showed how strongly he objected.
examples.zh: 他憤慨的回答顯示出他強烈反對。

explains.en: This adjective describes someone who feels angry because something seems unfair or wrong. A person may react strongly to an insult. The feeling reflects moral offense.
A character may speak sharply after seeing someone treated badly. Their anger is directed at an injustice. The word conveys offended outrage.
People may feel this way when a rule is applied unfairly. The reaction is stronger than simple annoyance. It expresses a sense that something is not right.

examples.en: The warm sunlight induced a feeling of calm.
examples.zh: 溫暖的陽光帶來了平靜的感覺。

examples.en: The teacher induced the class to ask more questions.
examples.zh: 老師鼓勵全班提出更多問題。

examples.en: The speech induced laughter from the audience.
examples.zh: 這場演講逗得觀眾發笑。

explains.en: This verb means to cause a particular event, action, or feeling. A smell may bring back a memory. One thing leads to another.
A medicine may cause sleepiness in some people. The effect follows after it is taken. The word appears in formal descriptions of causes.
A person can persuade someone to do something. Kind words may lead a friend to join a game. This use means to bring about an action.

examples.en: The region began to industrialize after the new railway opened.
examples.zh: 新鐵路通車後，這個地區開始工業化。

examples.en: The country industrialized rapidly during the last century.
examples.zh: 這個國家在上個世紀迅速工業化。

examples.en: Plans to industrialize the valley faced local opposition.
examples.zh: 讓山谷地區工業化的計畫遭到當地反對。

explains.en: This verb means to develop factories and machine-based production in a place. A small farming town may begin making goods. The economy changes over time.
New roads and plants may appear as a region builds its manufacturing base. More people may move there for work. The verb describes that broad change.
A country can shift from mostly farm work to factory work. This process changes jobs and daily life. It is a large social and economic development.

examples.en: The nurse explained that the illness was infectious.
examples.zh: 護理師說明這種疾病會傳染。

examples.en: An infectious laugh filled the room.
examples.zh: 富有感染力的笑聲充滿整個房間。

examples.en: The school sent home a notice about an infectious disease.
examples.zh: 學校寄通知提醒家長注意傳染病。

entries.definition: （形）傳染性的；容易感染他人；也可形容情緒或笑聲很有感染力。

explains.en: This adjective describes something that can spread from one person or animal to another. A cold may pass through a classroom. Tiny germs can move between people.
A disease that spreads easily is described this way. Doctors may ask sick people to stay home. The word concerns how an illness passes between hosts.
The adjective can also describe a feeling or habit that quickly affects others. Laughter may spread through a room. This use is figurative.

examples.en: From the footprints, we inferred that someone had entered the garden.
examples.zh: 從腳印我們推斷有人進過花園。

examples.en: She inferred his mood from his quiet reply.
examples.zh: 她從他安靜的回答推知他的心情。

examples.en: The scientists infer the bird's route from tracking data.
examples.zh: 科學家根據追蹤資料推斷鳥的路線。

explains.en: This verb means to reach an idea by using clues and facts. A detective may notice muddy shoes near a door. The details point toward an answer.
A reader can work out a character's feelings from the way they speak. The writer may not state those feelings directly. Reasoning connects the clues.
Scientists draw conclusions from what they observe. New evidence can change their view. The verb describes a thoughtful conclusion rather than a wild guess.

examples.en: The rough edge inflicted a small cut on his hand.
examples.zh: 粗糙的邊緣在他手上劃出一道小傷口。

examples.en: The court inflicted a penalty for the violation.
examples.zh: 法院因違規行為施加了處罰。

examples.en: The storm inflicted serious damage on the harbor.
examples.zh: 暴風雨對港口造成嚴重損害。

explains.en: This verb means to cause pain, harm, or a penalty. A rough fall may hurt someone's knee. The action brings an unpleasant result.
A judge may give a punishment for breaking a rule. The penalty is placed on the person who did wrong. The verb often sounds formal.
A storm can cause damage to a town. The harm may affect homes or roads. This verb focuses on the action that causes it.

examples.en: Many birds inhabit the wetlands in spring.
examples.zh: 春天有許多鳥類棲息在濕地。

examples.en: A small family inhabits the cottage by the lake.
examples.zh: 一戶人家住在湖邊的小屋裡。

examples.en: Few plants inhabit the dry rocky slope.
examples.zh: 乾燥多石的山坡上幾乎沒有植物生長。

explains.en: This verb means to live in a particular place. People may make their homes in a town for many years. Animals can also live in forests.
A book may describe species that live in a certain region. Climate and food affect where they can survive. The verb identifies their home area.
The word sounds more formal than simply saying live. It focuses on where a person or animal has a home. The place can be a country or habitat.

examples.en: Each inhabitant received a card for the town library.
examples.zh: 每位居民都收到一張鎮立圖書館的借書證。

examples.en: The island has fewer than a hundred inhabitants.
examples.zh: 這座島上的居民不到一百人。

examples.en: A fox is a wild inhabitant of the forest.
examples.zh: 狐狸是森林中的野生住民。

entries.definition: （名）居民、棲居者；住在某地或生活於某處的生物。

explains.en: This noun means a person or animal that lives in a particular place. A village may have a few hundred people. Each one is a resident.
A forest can have many kinds of living creatures. Each species makes its home there. The term describes a local resident, human or animal.
A report may count the people living in a district. It can describe where they live. The word focuses on their connection to a place.

examples.en: The judge worked to correct the injustice.
examples.zh: 法官努力糾正這項不公義。

examples.en: They protested against the injustice of the rule.
examples.zh: 他們抗議這項規則的不公平。

examples.en: The story shows the injustice faced by poor families.
examples.zh: 故事呈現了貧困家庭遭遇的不公待遇。

entries.definition: 不公正；不公平的待遇；冤屈。

explains.en: This noun means a situation that is unfair or a wrong action. A rule may treat one group badly. People may ask for change.
A person who is denied a fair chance may experience this kind of wrong. The treatment harms someone. The word describes the lack of fairness.
History books may describe unfair laws or unequal treatment. Those events show that people were not treated justly. The noun names such a wrong.

examples.en: The inland village rarely sees strong sea winds.
examples.zh: 內陸村莊很少遇到強勁海風。

examples.en: They traveled inland from the coast.
examples.zh: 他們從海岸往內陸旅行。

examples.en: The inland lake is surrounded by hills.
examples.zh: 這座內陸湖被群山環繞。

entries.definition: （形）內陸的；（副）向內陸；（名）內陸地區

explains.en: This adjective describes an area away from the coast. A town near the middle of a country is far from the sea. The word tells where it lies.
It can also describe movement from the shore toward the interior. A boat may travel toward land. The direction is away from open water.
People may contrast areas far from the coast with coastal areas. A country’s interior is away from the sea. Maps can show the region beyond the shoreline.

examples.en: Innumerable stars filled the clear night sky.
examples.zh: 無數星星點綴著晴朗的夜空。

examples.en: The old tree had innumerable tiny leaves.
examples.zh: 那棵老樹長著無數細小的葉子。

examples.en: She thanked the innumerable people who helped.
examples.zh: 她感謝了無數伸出援手的人。

explains.en: This adjective means too many to count easily. A dark sky may show a great many stars. The exact total is not important.
A library may hold a huge number of books. Counting each one would take a long time. The word emphasizes great quantity.
The term is often used for many small objects or events. A beach can hold countless grains of sand. It conveys abundance rather than an exact number.

examples.en: I called to inquire about the class schedule.
examples.zh: 我打電話詢問課程時間表。

examples.en: The reporter inquired about the missing records.
examples.zh: 記者詢問了遺失紀錄的情況。

examples.en: She inquired whether the museum was open.
examples.zh: 她詢問博物館是否開放。

entries.definition: （動）詢問、查詢；提出問題以取得資訊。

explains.en: This verb means to ask for information. A traveler may ask where the station is. The question helps them learn something.
It can also mean to investigate or seek details. A reporter may ask about a decision. Careful questions can reveal facts.
The word sounds more formal than simply ask. A person may contact an office to learn about a schedule. The verb describes seeking information.

examples.en: Her insistence on a clear answer surprised the group.
examples.zh: 她堅持要得到明確答覆，讓大家感到意外。

examples.en: His insistence that we leave early proved wise.
examples.zh: 他堅持提早出發，後來證明是明智的。

examples.en: The child's insistence continued through dinner.
examples.zh: 那個孩子整頓晚餐都不斷堅持自己的要求。

entries.definition: 堅持；堅決主張；堅持要求。

explains.en: This noun means the act of firmly repeating a demand or belief. A child may keep asking to stay up late. The request does not easily stop.
A person may strongly state that something must happen. The repeated statement shows determination. It can sometimes sound forceful to listeners.
The word can describe a quality of steady demand. A teacher may insist that students listen carefully. The noun focuses on firm persistence.

examples.en: Her instinctive response was to protect the kitten.
examples.zh: 她本能地做出保護小貓的反應。

examples.en: The dog's instinctive reaction was to bark.
examples.zh: 那隻狗本能地吠叫起來。

examples.en: He made an instinctive move to catch the falling cup.
examples.zh: 他本能地伸手接住快掉下的杯子。

entries.definition: （形）本能的；出於直覺的；不經思考的

explains.en: This adjective describes a reaction that happens naturally, without careful thought. A person may pull a hand away from a hot surface. The body responds quickly.
A newborn may turn toward a gentle touch near the cheek. The response happens without lessons or careful planning. It is a natural reaction rather than a practiced habit.
Animals often act from natural patterns of behavior. A bird may protect its nest when danger appears. The adjective describes an unplanned reaction.

examples.en: Active weightlifters aim for daily protein intake of 1.6 to 2.2 grams per kilogram.
examples.zh: 規律進行高強度重訓的巨巨每日建議蛋白質攝取量為每公斤體重一至兩倍以上。

examples.en: Keep a food diary to make sure your daily caloric intake aligns with your weight targets.
examples.zh: 記錄飲食日記能確保你每日的總熱量攝取量與設定的減重或增肌目標保持一致。

examples.en: Increasing your dietary fiber and water intake helps keep you satiated throughout the day.
examples.zh: 增加日常飲食中的膳食纖維與飲水量攝取，能幫助你整天維持良好的飽足感。

explains.en: This noun means the amount of food, drink, or material taken into the body or a system. A daily food total can be counted. Doctors may discuss a person’s diet.
A machine may have an air or water amount entering it. The quantity affects how the system works. The word names what comes in.
A school may welcome a new group of students each autumn. The term can mean the people accepted during one period. Here, it refers to those entering an organization.

examples.en: Her intellect helped her solve the difficult puzzle.
examples.zh: 她的才智幫助她解開了這道難題。

examples.en: The book challenges the intellect of its readers.
examples.zh: 這本書挑戰讀者的智力。

examples.en: He admired her sharp intellect and curiosity.
examples.zh: 他欣賞她敏銳的才智與好奇心。

explains.en: This noun means the ability to think, learn, and understand. A person may solve complex problems. The quality includes reasoning and memory.
A scholar may be known for strong thinking skills. Reading and study can develop knowledge, but this noun focuses on mental ability. It is not the same as facts alone.
The mind uses this ability to compare ideas and find patterns. A difficult puzzle can test how well someone reasons. This sense refers to thinking power rather than stored facts.

examples.en: The interpreter helped the visitors speak with the guide.
examples.zh: 口譯員協助訪客與導覽員溝通。

examples.en: An interpreter translated the doctor's questions.
examples.zh: 口譯員翻譯了醫師的問題。

examples.en: The conference hired an interpreter for each language.
examples.zh: 會議為每種語言聘請了一位口譯員。

entries.definition: （名）口譯員、解說者；即時轉換語言或說明意思的人。

explains.en: This is a person who helps people using different languages understand each other as they communicate. The person works with spoken words or signs made with the hands. Written documents are usually handled by a translator.
At a meeting, this worker may repeat each speaker’s meaning in another language. Everyone can follow the discussion. The work requires language skill.
A book can be changed into a different language by a translator. The meaning and style should remain clear. The noun refers to the person who helps with spoken or signed communication.

examples.en: Turn left at the next intersection.
examples.zh: 在下一個十字路口左轉。

examples.en: A traffic light controls the busy intersection.
examples.zh: 交通號誌管理這個繁忙的十字路口。

examples.en: The accident happened at a quiet intersection.
examples.zh: 事故發生在一個安靜的交叉路口。

explains.en: This noun means a place where two or more roads cross. Traffic may stop there for a light. Drivers choose which direction to go.
A pedestrian can cross from one street to another at this point. Signs and signals help people move safely. The roads meet in one location.
The word can also describe where lines or ideas meet. A map may show a rail route and road meeting. It names a crossing point.

examples.en: A neighbor intervened when the children began to argue.
examples.zh: 孩子們開始爭吵時，鄰居介入了。

examples.en: The manager intervened to resolve the problem.
examples.zh: 經理介入解決問題。

examples.en: Nothing intervened between the first visit and the next.
examples.zh: 第一次拜訪和下次拜訪之間沒有發生其他事情。

entries.definition: （動）介入；干預；發生於兩件事之間

explains.en: This verb means to step into a situation to help or change what is happening. A teacher may stop an argument between students. The action affects the event.
A government may become involved in a dispute between groups. The goal may be to settle the problem. The verb describes taking an active role.
It can also mean that an event happens between two times. A short break may occur during a long trip. Context distinguishes involvement from something in between.

examples.en: Curved terraced balconies foster acoustic intimacy, connecting patrons intimately with solo violinists.
examples.zh: 微弧形梯田包廂營造出極佳的「視聽親密感」（Intimacy），拉近了全場聽眾與小提琴獨奏家的心靈距離。

examples.en: Sharing heartfelt hopes and vulnerabilities deepens emotional intimacy between lifelong romantic partners.
examples.zh: 彼此毫無保留地分享心底深處的願景與脆弱，能深刻加深終身伴侶之間細水長流的情感親密連結。

examples.en: The coffee shop’s dim lighting and plush corner booths provide a sense of cozy conversational intimacy.
examples.zh: 街角咖啡館柔和昏黃的暖色照明與角落舒適的絨布卡座，營造出一種溫馨放鬆的私密談心氛圍。

entries.definition: 縮短舞台與觀眾席心理距離之視聽親密感；親密

explains.en: This noun means a close, private bond between people. Friends may share personal thoughts. Trust helps the relationship grow.
It can also refer to a private or cozy atmosphere. A small room with soft light may feel warm. The word describes closeness and comfort.
The term may describe deep personal knowledge or familiarity. People who have known each other for years may feel close. It can refer to emotional closeness or privacy.

examples.en: The older students tried to intimidate the new team.
examples.zh: 年長的學生試圖嚇唬新加入的隊伍。

examples.en: A barking dog intimidated the little boy.
examples.zh: 吠叫的狗嚇到了小男孩。

examples.en: She was not intimidated by the difficult questions.
examples.zh: 她沒有被那些難題嚇倒。

explains.en: This verb means to make someone feel afraid or less confident. A loud voice may scare a new student. The person may hesitate to speak.
A large opponent can make a smaller player feel nervous. Their size or behavior may seem threatening. The verb describes causing fear or pressure.
The action can happen without physical harm. Strong language or a powerful position may make someone feel unable to respond. The word focuses on the effect of fear.

examples.en: Mastering natural rising and falling intonation conveys subtle humor, sarcasm, and warmth.
examples.zh: 熟練掌握英語自然生動的升降語調抑揚頓挫，能精準傳遞幽默、反諷與真誠溫暖的豐富情緒層次。

examples.en: Asking polite questions usually features a gentle rising intonation at the end of the sentence.
examples.zh: 在使用英語表達禮貌詢問或尋求對方確認時，句尾通常自然帶有微微上揚的輕柔升調。

examples.en: Flat, robotic intonation often causes international listeners to perceive the speaker as uninterested.
examples.zh: 平淡毫無抑揚頓挫的機器人死板語調，極易讓跨國會議中的外籍聽眾誤以為講者冷漠且心不在焉。

examples.en: Flawless guitar intonation means harmonics at the twelfth fret match fretted notes with zero beating.
examples.zh: 完美無瑕的「全把位音準」（Intonation），代表第十二品的泛音與實音音高完全一致且毫無拍頻干擾。

examples.en: Subtle changes in vocal intonation revealed the witness’s growing nervousness on the witness stand.
examples.zh: 證人語氣與聲調起伏中微小的情緒顫抖，無意間透露出其在證人席上內心深處日益加劇的恐懼與緊張。

examples.en: Adjusting electric guitar saddle screws fine-tunes string length to achieve spot-on pitch intonation.
examples.zh: 旋轉電吉他下弦枕調節螺絲能微調琴弦有效震動長度，從而使整把琴的八度音準達到毫釐不差。

entries.definition: 英語語調升降起伏；抑揚頓挫；全把位絕對精準十二平均律八度音院校準；聲調

explains.en: This noun means the rise and fall of a speaker's voice. Questions may end with a higher sound. The pattern can change a sentence's feeling.
A storyteller can use voice patterns to show excitement or sadness. Listeners learn meaning from more than words. The sound shape helps communicate emotion.
Language learners may practice how their voices move while speaking. Different patterns can signal a question or statement. The noun names this vocal pattern.

examples.en: The strange map intrigued the young explorer.
examples.zh: 奇怪的地圖引起了年輕探險家的好奇。

examples.en: The mystery intrigued every reader in the club.
examples.zh: 謎團讓讀書會裡的每個人都很感興趣。

examples.en: The plot intrigued her from the first page.
examples.zh: 她從第一頁就被情節吸引。

entries.definition: （名）陰謀、密謀；（動）引起好奇、使著迷。

explains.en: As a verb, this means to make someone very interested or curious. A mystery may keep readers guessing. They want to know what happens next.
It can also mean to secretly plan or plot. A character may work with another person to arrange an event. This use can suggest something suspicious.
As a noun, it can refer to a secret plan or a strong interest. The context tells whether it describes curiosity or a hidden scheme. The sentence context reveals the intended meaning.

examples.en: Please knock before you intrude on their meeting.
examples.zh: 要打擾他們開會前，請先敲門。

examples.en: The reporter did not want to intrude on the family's grief.
examples.zh: 記者不想打擾這家人悲傷的時刻。

examples.en: A loud sound intruded into the quiet room.
examples.zh: 一聲巨響打破了房間的寧靜。

explains.en: This verb means to enter a place or conversation without being invited. Someone may walk into a private room. The action can seem rude.
A person may interrupt a quiet moment by joining without permission. Others may feel their privacy has been broken. The verb describes crossing a social boundary.
The word can also describe unwanted entry into a space. A visitor should wait before entering. It often carries a negative tone.

examples.en: The intruder ran away when the lights came on.
examples.zh: 燈亮起時，闖入者逃走了。

examples.en: A security guard stopped the intruder at the gate.
examples.zh: 警衛在大門口攔住了闖入者。

examples.en: The family heard an intruder in the garage.
examples.zh: 這家人聽見車庫裡有闖入者。

entries.definition: （名）闖入者；未經許可進入的人

explains.en: This noun means a person who enters a place without permission. A homeowner may find someone in a locked yard. The person is not welcome there.
In a story, a stranger may enter a private room secretly. The character's presence creates worry. The noun names the person who crossed the boundary.
The word can also describe something unwanted that enters a place, such as noise. The main idea is an unwelcome arrival. Context determines whether it is a person or thing.

examples.en: Your notes were invaluable during the review.
examples.zh: 你的筆記在複習時非常有用。

examples.en: The guide's advice proved invaluable to the travelers.
examples.zh: 導遊的建議對旅客來說極有價值。

examples.en: Her experience was invaluable to the project.
examples.zh: 她的經驗對這個專案非常寶貴。

explains.en: This adjective means extremely useful or valuable. A map is very helpful when roads are unfamiliar. Its worth is clear during the trip.
A person who gives timely help may be described this way. Their support matters greatly. The word emphasizes high value, not a money price.
A piece of information can be extremely useful for solving a problem. It may save time or prevent confusion. The adjective praises its importance.

examples.en: He invariably takes the window seat.
examples.zh: 他總是坐靠窗的位子。

examples.en: The shop invariably closes at six.
examples.zh: 這家店一向在六點關門。

examples.en: She invariably smiles when she sees her dog.
examples.zh: 她每次看到自己的狗都會笑。

entries.definition: （副）總是、一向如此；每次都以相同方式發生。

explains.en: This adverb means something happens every time or almost every time. A clock may show the same time each morning. The pattern is steady.
A person may always choose the same seat in class. The repeated choice happens with little change. This word describes regular behavior.
This is stronger than usually because it says something happens every time. A clock may chime whenever the hour changes. The word describes a pattern with no exceptions.

examples.en: Supermarkets perform regular inventory counts to replenish empty shelves.
examples.zh: 超級市場定期盤點庫存以適時為空貨架補貨。

examples.en: Barcode scanners help workers track warehouse inventory with pinpoint precision.
examples.zh: 條碼雷射掃描槍協助倉儲盤點人員以無比精確的精準度實時追蹤倉庫存貨。

examples.en: Excessive surplus inventory forces department stores to hold deep clearance sales.
examples.zh: 龐大過剩的積壓庫存促使各大百貨商場不得不祭出破盤下殺的清倉特賣。

examples.en: Expand your bag storage limit when your adventure inventory runs out of space.
examples.zh: 當您的隨身冒險背包物品欄空間告急時，可使用背包擴充券加大格子容量。

examples.en: The retail store shuts down annually for two days to take a full stock inventory.
examples.zh: 這家大型服飾連鎖店每年皆會暫停營業兩天，由全體員工進行全門市商品實體盤點。

examples.en: Always organize your potion inventory carefully so you can heal quickly in combat.
examples.zh: 在踏入險境前請務必將背包欄位中的補血補魔藥水整理就緒，以便在激烈交鋒時秒速回血。

examples.en: Real-time cloud software tracks inventory levels across all retail stores and central warehouses.
examples.zh: 雲端 ERP 即時進銷存系統能同步動態監控全台數百家連鎖實體門市與中央大倉的庫存水位。

examples.en: Conducting an annual physical inventory count helps accounting verify discrepancies with system records.
examples.zh: 每年定期舉行全公司實體庫存全面盤點，有助於會計部門確實稽核實體存貨與系統帳面數字的差異。

examples.en: Lean manufacturing models minimize idle inventory to reduce costly warehouse storage overhead.
examples.zh: 精實生產管理模式致力於將閒置在庫庫存降至最低，從而大幅削減高昂的倉儲空間與租金負擔。

examples.en: Listed enterprises conduct annual greenhouse gas inventories adhering strictly to ISO 14064 standards.
examples.zh: 台灣全體上市櫃企業每年皆需遵循 ISO 14064 國際標準，嚴謹完成組織型溫室氣體碳排盤查。

examples.en: Store managers conducted a thorough physical inventory check before the annual clearance sale.
examples.zh: 門市店長在年終換季出清特賣會前夕，帶領全體同仁連夜進行了徹底的實體門市庫存盤點造冊。

examples.en: The warehouse implemented barcode scanners to track electronic component inventory in real time.
examples.zh: 物流倉儲全面導入手持式條碼雷射掃描槍，以即時掌控數萬項電子零組件的精準進出庫庫存清冊。

entries.definition: 存貨；庫存清單；背包物品欄；庫存盤點；存貨清冊；企業溫室氣體排碳盤查

explains.en: This noun means a detailed list of goods, supplies, or items held by a person or business. A shop counts its products. The list helps track what is available.
A warehouse may record every box and its location. Staff use the record to know what is in storage. The noun can mean the list or the goods themselves.
A person may keep a list of possessions before a trip. This helps them remember what they packed. The word concerns an organized count of items.

examples.en: It was ironic that the lifeguard forgot how to swim.
examples.zh: 諷刺的是，救生員竟然忘了怎麼游泳。

examples.en: The ironic ending made everyone laugh.
examples.zh: 這個出人意料的結局讓大家都笑了。

examples.en: She made an ironic comment about the rainy picnic.
examples.zh: 她對下雨天的野餐說了一句反諷的話。

entries.definition: 諷刺的；具有反差意味的；反語的。

explains.en: This adjective describes a result that is strange because it is opposite to what people expect. A fire station may burn down. The contrast feels surprising.
A person may say something that means the opposite of its literal words. The listener understands the real message from the situation or tone. The contrast can be humorous.
The word can also describe a situation where an outcome clashes with what seems reasonable. A lifeguard who cannot swim is a surprising mismatch. Context determines the kind of contrast.

examples.en: The irritable child wanted a quiet place to rest.
examples.zh: 那個容易煩躁的孩子想找個安靜的地方休息。

examples.en: Bright lights made his eyes irritable.
examples.zh: 強光讓他的眼睛感到不適。

examples.en: She felt irritable after a night with little sleep.
examples.zh: 睡眠不足的一夜後，她感到容易煩躁。

entries.definition: （形）易怒的；煩躁的；容易受刺激的

explains.en: This adjective describes someone who becomes annoyed easily. A small noise may upset them. Their patience is short.
A tired person may react sharply to a simple question. Lack of rest can affect mood. The word describes a tendency to feel irritation.
The term can describe a body part that reacts painfully to touch or light. A person's skin may feel sensitive. Context shows whether it is about mood or the body.

examples.en: The scratchy label began to irritate her neck.
examples.zh: 粗糙的標籤開始磨得她的脖子發癢。

examples.en: The loud alarm irritated the neighbors.
examples.zh: 刺耳的警報聲惹惱了鄰居。

examples.en: Dust can irritate a person's eyes.
examples.zh: 灰塵可能刺激人的眼睛。

explains.en: This verb means to bother someone or make them feel annoyed. A buzzing fly can disturb a person trying to read. The effect may be small but unpleasant.
A rough tag may make the skin feel uncomfortable. The body reacts with annoyance or pain. The word can describe mental or physical discomfort.
A repeated sound may bother someone more each time it happens. The verb describes causing that unpleasant reaction. The cause may be a person, thing, or action.

examples.en: They rented a cottage on a quiet isle.
examples.zh: 他們在一座寧靜的小島上租了一間小屋。

examples.en: The boat circled the rocky isle.
examples.zh: 小船繞著岩石小島航行。

examples.en: A lighthouse stood on the distant isle.
examples.zh: 一座燈塔矗立在遠方的小島上。

entries.definition: （名）小島；一片被水環繞的陸地。

explains.en: This noun means a small island, especially one near a coast. A boat may carry visitors there. It is surrounded by water on all sides.
A map may show a chain of small land areas near the shore. Each one can be called by this term. Some are inhabited, while others are empty.
The word is often used in place names and travel writing. It usually suggests a small island rather than a large country. Context may identify its location.

examples.en: The mosquito bite left an itch on her arm.
examples.zh: 蚊子叮咬後，她的手臂發癢。

examples.en: My eyes itch when pollen fills the air.
examples.zh: 空氣中花粉多時，我的眼睛會發癢。

examples.en: He had an itch to explore the old lighthouse.
examples.zh: 他很想去探索那座老燈塔。

explains.en: As a noun, this is an uncomfortable feeling on the skin that makes someone want to scratch. An insect bite can cause it. The sensation may be brief or lasting.
As a verb, it means to feel this sensation or to scratch because of it. A wool sweater may bother the skin. The action can relieve the feeling for a moment.
The word can also describe a strong desire to do something. Someone may feel eager to travel. In that sense, it is a figurative craving.

examples.en: Ivy covered part of the stone wall.
examples.zh: 常春藤覆蓋了石牆的一部分。

examples.en: The old house was hidden by ivy.
examples.zh: 老房子被常春藤遮住了。

examples.en: She planted ivy beside the garden gate.
examples.zh: 她在花園大門旁種了常春藤。

entries.definition: （名）常春藤；攀附牆面生長的藤本植物

explains.en: This noun names a climbing plant with dark green leaves. It can grow along walls or tree trunks. Some kinds keep their leaves through winter.
The plant often grows in shaded places. Its small roots help it cling to surfaces. Gardeners may use it to cover a fence.
In stories, the plant can symbolize loyalty or long life because it stays green. Its leaves have several pointed lobes. The noun refers to the plant.

examples.en: The jade pendant was a gift from her grandmother.
examples.zh: 那塊玉墜是祖母送給她的禮物。

examples.en: A jade carving rested in the glass case.
examples.zh: 一件玉雕擺放在玻璃櫃裡。

examples.en: The vase had a soft jade color.
examples.zh: 花瓶呈現柔和的玉綠色。

explains.en: This noun names a hard green stone used in jewelry and carvings. It can be polished until it shines. Many cultures value it highly.
The stone may be cut into beads, statues, or small ornaments. Its color can range from pale to deep green. The material is durable.
The word can also name a color similar to the green stone. A scarf may have that rich shade. Context indicates whether it means the gem or hue.

examples.en: The janitor unlocked the school gym.
examples.zh: 管理員打開了學校體育館的門。

examples.en: Our janitor fixed the broken classroom clock.
examples.zh: 學校管理員修好了教室裡壞掉的時鐘。

examples.en: The janitor swept the hallway after lunch.
examples.zh: 午餐後，清潔管理員掃了走廊。

entries.definition: （名）管理員、清潔工；負責照看建築物與維持整潔的人。

explains.en: This noun names a person whose job is to clean and care for a building. The worker may sweep halls and empty bins. Schools often employ someone in this role.
A building worker may repair a loose door handle or move furniture. The exact duties depend on the workplace. The term often describes a school caretaker.
People may see this worker opening rooms early in the morning. The person keeps the place orderly and working. The noun names the job holder.

examples.en: Jasmine flowers scented the evening air.
examples.zh: 茉莉花的香氣瀰漫在夜晚的空氣中。

examples.en: She added jasmine blossoms to the tea.
examples.zh: 她在茶裡加入茉莉花。

examples.en: A jasmine vine climbed the garden trellis.
examples.zh: 一株茉莉藤攀上花園的棚架。

explains.en: This noun names a plant with small white flowers that have a sweet smell. Its leaves are usually dark green. The blossoms are used in tea and perfume.
The scent is strongest in the evening for some kinds. A garden may grow this plant beside a path. The flowers can be picked for decoration.
The word can also refer to the fragrance of the flowers. Tea makers use the blossoms to add flavor. It is a familiar garden plant in warm regions.

examples.en: The keys made a jingle in his pocket.
examples.zh: 鑰匙在他口袋裡發出叮噹聲。

examples.en: A bell jingled when the door opened.
examples.zh: 門一開，鈴鐺就叮噹作響。

examples.en: The short advertisement jingle stayed in my head.
examples.zh: 那段簡短的廣告旋律一直留在我腦海裡。

entries.definition: （名）叮噹聲；短促旋律；（動）發出叮噹聲

explains.en: As a noun, this is a short ringing or repeated sound. Small bells may make it as they move. It can also name a catchy tune.
As a verb, it means to make such a sound or to repeat words in a sing-song way. A phone may ring with a bright tone. The sound is easy to notice.
A familiar phrase may stay in someone's mind because it has a repeating rhythm. The word can describe that remembered sound pattern. Context shows whether it is a sound or phrase.

examples.en: The jockey guided the horse around the final turn.
examples.zh: 騎師引導賽馬通過最後一個彎道。

examples.en: She hopes to become a jockey one day.
examples.zh: 她希望有一天能成為賽馬騎師。

examples.en: The politician's aide jockeyed for influence.
examples.zh: 那名政治人物的助理努力爭取影響力。

entries.definition: （名）賽馬騎師；（動）操縱；爭奪有利位置

explains.en: As a noun, this is a person who rides and trains racehorses. The rider must be light and skilled. Horse races depend on both rider and animal.
As a verb, it can mean to compete in horse races or ride as a professional. A young rider may train for events. The work requires balance and courage.
The word also appears in the phrase for a person who controls a political contest behind the scenes. The term can suggest influence or maneuvering. The rider works to gain a better position.

examples.en: The jolly baker sang while making bread.
examples.zh: 那位快樂的麵包師一邊做麵包一邊唱歌。

examples.en: She greeted us jolly and warmly.
examples.zh: 她愉快又熱情地向我們打招呼。

examples.en: His jokes made the whole table jolly.
examples.zh: 他的笑話讓整桌的人都開心起來。

entries.definition: （形）愉快的、快樂的；（副）非常（較舊用法）；（動）取笑。

explains.en: This adjective means cheerful and full of good humor. A person may tell funny stories at a gathering. Their mood lifts the group.
As an adverb, it can describe doing something in a happy way. A singer may greet the audience with a bright voice. The manner feels friendly.
The word can also be a noun for a cheerful person or a verb meaning to make someone happy. Context tells which form is being used. It may describe mood or action.

examples.en: The joyous crowd cheered for the team.
examples.zh: 歡欣的人群為球隊歡呼。

examples.en: It was a joyous reunion after many years.
examples.zh: 多年後的重逢令人喜悅。

examples.en: The children danced in a joyous circle.
examples.zh: 孩子們在歡樂的圈子裡跳舞。

explains.en: This adjective means very happy and full of delight. A child may feel this way on a birthday. The emotion is strong and bright.
A group may celebrate a success with excited smiles. The mood feels joyful rather than quiet. The word describes deep happiness.
Music or a kind surprise can create this feeling. People may share their excitement with others. The adjective emphasizes delight and pleasure.

examples.en: An ultra-thin aluminum oxide insulator forms the non-linear Josephson junction at the heart of each transmon.
examples.zh: 夾在超導體中間的奈米級氧化鋁絕緣薄膜，構成了超導晶片最核心的約瑟夫森接面。

examples.en: Quantum tunneling of Cooper pairs across the Josephson junction generates non-linear inductance.
examples.zh: 庫柏電子對穿越約瑟夫森接面發生的量子穿隧效應，在電路中產生了無價的非線性電感特性。

examples.en: Precision electron-beam lithography guarantees uniform junction thickness across the entire chip.
examples.zh: 高精度電子束微影技術，確保了整片晶圓上數千顆約瑟夫森接面絕緣層厚度達到原子級的一致性。

entries.definition: 約瑟夫森接面 (超導量子晶片核心)；接合點

explains.en: This noun means a place where roads, lines, or paths meet. Drivers may turn in several directions there. Signs help them choose a route.
A railway line may connect with another at a specific point. Trains can switch paths at this meeting place. The term describes that connection.
The word can also refer to a connection between ideas or systems. A discussion may bring two topics together. It names a point where things join.

examples.en: She visited her kin during the holidays.
examples.zh: 她在假期探望了親戚。

examples.en: The story tells of kin separated by war.
examples.zh: 這個故事講述被戰爭分離的親人。

examples.en: Those two languages are kin to one another.
examples.zh: 那兩種語言彼此相關。

explains.en: This noun means family members or relatives. People may gather with their relatives for a holiday. The word often sounds formal or old-fashioned.
It can also refer to a group of related people or animals. A wolf pack may include close family members. The term emphasizes shared ancestry.
As an adjective, it means related or similar. Two languages may share a common origin. The context shows whether the word names family or connection.

examples.en: Dry leaves helped kindle the campfire.
examples.zh: 乾樹葉幫助點燃營火。

examples.en: Her question kindled a lively discussion.
examples.zh: 她的問題引發了一場熱烈討論。

examples.en: The story kindled his interest in space.
examples.zh: 這個故事點燃了他對太空的興趣。

explains.en: This verb means to start a fire or make something begin to burn. A match can start a small flame. The fire may spread to dry wood.
It can also mean to cause a feeling or interest to begin. A book may spark curiosity in a child. The idea becomes active in the mind.
A person may encourage another to act or feel hopeful. A story can inspire courage. The verb can describe lighting a flame or starting an emotion.

examples.en: Our knowledgeable guide explained the old bridge's history.
examples.zh: 知識豐富的導覽員解說了那座古橋的歷史。

examples.en: She is knowledgeable about marine animals.
examples.zh: 她對海洋動物很了解。

examples.en: Ask the knowledgeable librarian for help.
examples.zh: 請向知識豐富的圖書館員求助。

entries.definition: （形）知識豐富的、博學的；對某主題有充分了解。

explains.en: This adjective describes someone who knows a lot about a subject. A mechanic may understand engines well. Experience and study build that knowledge.
A person can answer many questions about local history. Their information comes from reading or practice. The word praises a strong understanding.
The term can also describe a community or group with much information. A guide may know every path in a forest. Context tells what subject is understood.

examples.en: The lad carried a basket of apples.
examples.zh: 那名少年提著一籃蘋果。

examples.en: A cheerful lad waved from the gate.
examples.zh: 一名愉快的年輕人從大門口揮手。

examples.en: The old story follows a poor country lad.
examples.zh: 這個古老故事描述一名貧困的鄉村少年。

explains.en: This noun is an informal word for a boy or young man. A father may call his son this in a friendly way. It is less formal than young man.
A story set in the countryside may use the term for a farm boy. The meaning can depend on region and tone. It often sounds casual.
The word appears in some expressions for a young man who is learning a job. A new worker may be addressed this way. It can sound old-fashioned.

examples.en: The landlady repaired the leaking kitchen tap.
examples.zh: 女房東修好了漏水的廚房水龍頭。

examples.en: Our landlady welcomed us with fresh fruit.
examples.zh: 女房東用新鮮水果招待我們。

examples.en: The landlady collected the rent on Friday.
examples.zh: 女房東星期五收取房租。

entries.definition: （名）女房東；出租房屋的女性屋主

explains.en: This noun means a woman who owns or manages a rented house or apartment. A renter may contact her about a repair. She is responsible for the property.
In an inn or boarding house, she may welcome guests and arrange rooms. The word names the female owner or host. It is a traditional term.
A person may use this title when speaking politely to the woman in charge of a place to stay. The exact role depends on the setting. It is used in formal introductions.

examples.en: Heavy rain loosened mountain slopes, causing a massive hillside landslide.
examples.zh: 連日豪雨導致山坡土石鬆動，引發了大規模的山崩落石災情。

examples.en: Bulldozers worked continuously to clear tons of mud and boulders after the road landslide.
examples.zh: 數十輛大型推土機日夜不間斷全速搶修作業，全力清理崩塌公路路面上堆積如山的泥沙巨石。

examples.en: The incumbent president won a historic landslide victory in the nationwide democratic elections.
examples.zh: 現任總統在這次全國民主大選中，憑藉著跨世代的壓倒性支持率贏得了歷史性的壓倒性大勝。

entries.definition: 山崩；落石；土石流；壓倒性大勝

explains.en: This noun means a large mass of earth and rocks sliding down a slope. Heavy rain may loosen the ground. The movement can bury roads or houses.
It can also describe a very large victory in an election. One candidate receives far more votes than others. The result is overwhelming.
The word refers to a sudden movement downhill or, figuratively, a result by a huge margin. Context tells whether it is a natural disaster or a win. This noun has both literal and figurative uses.

examples.en: The island lies at a low latitude.
examples.zh: 這座島位於低緯度地區。

examples.en: The map shows the latitude of each city.
examples.zh: 地圖標示了每座城市的緯度。

examples.en: The region's latitude affects its climate.
examples.zh: 該地區的緯度會影響氣候。

explains.en: This noun measures how far north or south a place is from the equator. Maps use lines that circle the Earth. The measurement is given in degrees.
A city near the equator has a low number. A place close to the poles has a high number. The lines help locate positions on a globe.
The word can also mean freedom to decide or act. A country may have the power to govern itself. Context determines whether it means a map measurement or freedom.

examples.en: They served a lavish meal for the wedding guests.
examples.zh: 他們為婚宴賓客準備了豐盛的餐點。

examples.en: The palace had lavish decorations.
examples.zh: 宮殿裡有華麗的裝飾。

examples.en: She gave her friend a lavish birthday gift.
examples.zh: 她送給朋友一份豐厚的生日禮物。

entries.definition: （形）豪華的、豐富的；（動）大量給予或花費。

explains.en: This adjective describes something generous, rich, or large in amount. A host may prepare a large meal for guests. The amount is more than usual.
A person may spend money freely on decorations. The result looks rich and impressive. The word can describe spending, gifts, or style.
The term can also mean richly decorated or grand. A room may have soft carpets and bright ornaments. It suggests abundance and luxury.

examples.en: A layman asked the engineer to explain the bridge design.
examples.zh: 一名外行請工程師解釋橋梁設計。

examples.en: The guide explained the rules in terms a layman could understand.
examples.zh: 導覽員用外行人也能理解的方式解釋規則。

examples.en: A layman helped organize the church event.
examples.zh: 一位非神職人員協助籌辦教會活動。

entries.definition: 外行；非專業人士；平信徒。

explains.en: This noun means a person without expert training in a particular field. A writer may know a little about astronomy but not work as a scientist. The person is not a specialist.
The term can also describe a member of a religious community who is not a priest or minister. The person may still be active in the faith. The distinction concerns the person’s role.
It often contrasts with an expert or professional. A beginner may ask a specialist to explain complex ideas. The word identifies someone outside the professional role.

examples.en: The efficient apartment layout features three square bedrooms and two full bathrooms.
examples.zh: 這間房屋格局方正採光極佳，規劃有標準三房兩廳兩衛，動線流暢毫不浪費空間。

examples.en: An open-concept kitchen and living room layout makes small urban flats feel much larger.
examples.zh: 開放式廚房與無走道公領域的格局規劃，讓都會中小坪數空間在視覺上更顯開闊通透。

examples.en: The graphic designer adjusted the magazine page layout to balance images and typography.
examples.zh: 美編設計師細心調整了雜誌版面編排佈局，使精彩攝影圖片與文字排版達成完美平衡。

examples.en: Knocking down non-structural walls created an airy open-concept living room layout.
examples.zh: 果斷拆除非承重隔間牆，成功為室內營造出明亮通透、動線流暢的開放式客餐廳格局。

examples.en: The magazine graphic designer experimented with differing font sizes and multi-column layout styles.
examples.zh: 雜誌美編設計師大膽嘗試了不同的字體大小搭配與多欄式的現代雜誌排版版面格局。

examples.en: An efficient kitchen layout minimizes unnecessary steps between the refrigerator, sink, and stove.
examples.zh: 一套規劃合理的廚房黃金三角動線佈局，能極致減少冰箱、水槽與瓦斯爐之間的多餘步數走動。

entries.definition: 房屋格局；動線配置；版面編排；空間格局；平面配置動線；版面設計

explains.en: This noun means the way parts are arranged on a page, in a room, or in a building. A designer may place pictures and text. The arrangement affects how people use the space.
A home plan shows where rooms, doors, and windows are placed. A page plan shows where words and images appear. The term names this arrangement.
A worker may lay out chairs in rows before a meeting. A designer may decide where each chair should go. The noun names the planned arrangement.

examples.en: We signed a one-year apartment lease with the homeowner.
examples.zh: 我們與屋主簽署了一年的房屋租賃契約。

examples.en: The commercial retail lease expires at the end of next month.
examples.zh: 該商業店面租約將於下個月底正式到期屆滿。

examples.en: The company agreed to lease high-end office photocopiers from the supplier.
examples.zh: 該公司同意向供應商長期租賃高階辦公影印機。

examples.en: Read the residential lease contract carefully before signing and paying.
examples.zh: 在正式落筆簽署房屋租賃契約並支付款項前，請務必逐條詳閱租約條款。

examples.en: The commercial company signed a five-year lease for three floors in the new office tower.
examples.zh: 該跨國企業在新落成的摩天商辦大樓一口氣簽署了為期五年的三個樓層辦公室租約。

examples.en: The owner decided to lease out the ground floor storefront to a boutique bakery.
examples.zh: 屋主決定將位於一樓的黃金店面出租給一家精緻法式手工烘焙坊。

entries.definition: 租約；租期；出租；租賃合約

explains.en: As a noun, this is an agreement that lets someone use a home, car, or equipment for a set time in exchange for payment. The paper lists the terms. Both parties agree to its conditions.
As a verb, it means to pay to use property that belongs to someone else. A family may rent an apartment for a year. The owner receives regular payment.
The agreement can set how long the renter may stay and what costs are due. Both sides accept its conditions. The word names the contract or the act of renting.

examples.en: The legislator proposed a new road safety bill.
examples.zh: 這位立法者提出一項新的道路安全法案。

examples.en: Voters met the legislator at the town hall.
examples.zh: 選民在鎮公所與這位民意代表見面。

examples.en: The legislator spoke in favor of the proposal.
examples.zh: 這位立法委員發言支持這項提案。

entries.definition: （名）立法者；議員；制定法律的人

explains.en: This noun names a person elected or chosen to make laws for a government. The person debates proposals and votes. The role represents a district or group.
A city or national assembly may include many people in this role. They discuss public needs. Their work helps shape rules and policies.
Voters may choose this official during an election. The person serves for a set term. The noun refers to someone with lawmaking duties.

examples.en: The lengthy meeting ended after sunset.
examples.zh: 冗長的會議在日落後才結束。

examples.en: She wrote a lengthy letter to her cousin.
examples.zh: 她寫了一封很長的信給表親。

examples.en: The lengthy trip included several train changes.
examples.zh: 這趟漫長的旅程中途換了好幾次火車。

explains.en: This adjective describes something that takes a long time or has many words. A speech may continue for hours. The audience might lose focus.
A report with many pages can be difficult to finish. The information may be useful, but the length is great. This word describes its extended size.
A journey with many stops may feel long. The adjective can describe time, writing, or an explanation. It focuses on length rather than difficulty.

examples.en: The novel features a lesbian artist in Paris.
examples.zh: 這本小說描寫一位在巴黎生活的女同志藝術家。

examples.en: She is a lesbian who works as a nurse.
examples.zh: 她是一位從事護理工作的女同志。

examples.en: The documentary explores lesbian history.
examples.zh: 這部紀錄片探討女同志歷史。

entries.definition: （名）女同性戀者；（形）與女性同性戀者或其社群相關的。

explains.en: This noun or adjective describes a woman who is romantically or sexually attracted to other women. People may use the term as an identity. Each person can choose their own label.
The word can describe a woman or a relationship between women. It says who someone may love, not what hobbies or personality they have. The description concerns attraction.
The term appears in conversations about identity, family, and rights. Respectful language follows the words a person uses for herself. Context shows whether it is a noun or adjective.

examples.en: The medicine lessened the pain.
examples.zh: 藥物減輕了疼痛。

examples.en: A short break can lessen stress.
examples.zh: 短暫休息可以減輕壓力。

examples.en: The clouds lessened the afternoon heat.
examples.zh: 雲層減弱了午後的熱氣。

explains.en: This verb means to make something smaller, weaker, or less intense. A shade can reduce bright sunlight. The strong effect becomes milder.
A person may try to lower the amount of noise in a room. Closing a door can make the sound quieter. The action reduces the effect.
A difficult problem can become less serious over time. A small change may help. This verb describes making a degree or amount smaller.

examples.en: The snake has a lethal bite.
examples.zh: 這種蛇的咬傷可能致命。

examples.en: The story follows a search for a lethal poison.
examples.zh: 故事描述人們尋找一種致命毒藥。

examples.en: One lethal error ended the team's chances.
examples.zh: 一個致命的錯誤葬送了球隊的機會。

explains.en: This adjective means able to cause death or very serious harm. A dangerous poison can have this effect. The word signals extreme danger.
A weapon or disease may be described this way when it can kill. The risk is severe. The adjective is used in warnings and news reports.
The term can also describe a mistake that ruins an effort completely. A missed step may be disastrous for a plan. This figurative use means extremely harmful.

examples.en: The careless driver is held fully liable for all vehicle repair costs.
examples.zh: 該名疏忽肇事的駕駛人被依法判定須承擔全部車輛修繕賠償責任。

examples.en: Under product safety regulations, manufacturers are strictly liable for injuries caused by defective designs.
examples.zh: 依據現行消費者保護法規，製造大廠對於因產品先天設計不良瑕疵所釀成的消費者人身傷害負有嚴格責任。

examples.en: In rainy weather, mountain highways are liable to sudden rockfalls and landslides.
examples.zh: 在梅雨連綿或豪大雨來襲時，高山落石多發路段的公路極易發生無預警的邊坡崩塌與致命落石。

entries.definition: 負有法律責任的；應負責的

explains.en: This adjective means legally or morally responsible for something. A driver may have to pay for damage they caused. The responsibility can be financial.
It can also mean likely to do or experience something. A plant is likely to wilt without water. The word introduces a possible tendency.
A person may be responsible under a rule or contract. The details determine what they must do. The adjective can describe duty or likelihood.

examples.en: The rescuers liberated the trapped hikers.
examples.zh: 救援人員解救了受困的登山客。

examples.en: The country was liberated after years of occupation.
examples.zh: 經過多年的佔領後，這個國家獲得解放。

examples.en: The new schedule liberated her from late-night work.
examples.zh: 新的排班讓她不必再深夜工作。

explains.en: This verb means to set someone free from control, danger, or unfair limits. A prisoner may leave captivity. The person gains freedom.
A country may free itself from outside rule. The people gain control of their own decisions. The verb describes becoming independent.
It can also mean freeing someone from a burden or fear. A kind explanation may ease a worry. The word emphasizes release from a limit.

examples.en: The museum exhibit covers the liberation of the city.
examples.zh: 博物館展覽介紹了這座城市的解放。

examples.en: They celebrated their nation's liberation day.
examples.zh: 他們慶祝國家的解放日。

examples.en: The story describes liberation from an unfair rule.
examples.zh: 這個故事描述擺脫不公平統治的解放過程。

entries.definition: （名）解放、獲釋；使人或團體脫離控制或限制。

explains.en: This noun means the act of setting someone or a group free. A people may gain control over their own country. They are no longer ruled by another power.
It can also mean freedom from a difficult condition. A person may feel release after sharing a worry. The term describes becoming free.
A history book may describe the end of slavery or foreign rule. People gain rights and independence. The noun names that process or state.

examples.en: The lieutenant briefed the soldiers before sunrise.
examples.zh: 中尉在日出前向士兵們簡報。

examples.en: A lieutenant led the search team.
examples.zh: 一名中尉帶領搜索小隊。

examples.en: The police lieutenant spoke with the reporters.
examples.zh: 警察警官與記者交談。

explains.en: This noun is a military officer rank below captain and above sergeant in some forces. The exact level depends on the service. A person with this rank may lead a small group.
It is also used for a police officer who has a supervisory role. That officer may manage a team or station unit. The duties vary by location.
In some organizations, the title belongs to someone who helps a leader. The person may be second in command. The context determines the specific role.

examples.en: Lifelong learning keeps mature minds curious, confident, and socially connected with younger peers.
examples.zh: 堅持終身學習的精神，能讓長輩永遠對世界保持好奇心，自信跨越世代代溝。

examples.en: Reading great world literature is a lifelong habit that nourishes the human spirit and sharpens empathy.
examples.zh: 閱讀世界名著是一項受用終身的優良習慣，能時刻滋養心靈底蘊並深化同理共感力。
